This unified approach also allows us to resolve a problem posed by Shidlovskii: we obtain a general algebraic independence measure extending the classical Siegel-Lang measure to an arbitrary algebraically independent family of E-values. We also provide a short elementary proof of a second theorem of Andr{é}, which has become an important tool in the theory of Efunctions and concerns the primality of the specialization, at a regular point, of the ideal of functional relations of a vector of E-functions satisfying a differential system.

column6: Density and distribution of quotients associated with Goldring's $w$-function
column7: For primes $p,q,r$ that are not all equal, let $n=pqr$ and define Goldring's $w$-function by $w(n)=P(p+q)P(p+r)P(q+r)$, where $P(a)$ denotes the largest prime factor of $a$. In this paper, we resolve three problems of Chen, Shi and Wu. As $n\to\infty$ through such products, the sets of finite limit points of $P(w(n))/P(n)$ and $w(n)/n$ are $[0,1]$ and $[0,\infty)$, respectively. The same conclusions hold when $n$ is restricted either to $p^2q$ with distinct primes $p,q$ or to squarefree products of three primes. Nevertheless, on each of these three sets, the proportion of integers $n\le X$ satisfying $P(w(n))/P(n)>α$ tends to zero as $X\to\infty$, for every fixed $α>0$. We also determine the complete set of finite joint limit points of the two quotients for $n=p^2q$ with $p\ne q$.

column6: When GL(2) cusp forms meet CM points in GSp(4)
column7: Duke's equidistribution theorem shows that the nonconstant contribution of the $\mathrm{GL}(2)$ automorphic spectrum to CM packets becomes asymptotically negligible. CM packets on the Levi base index the fibers of Bessel quotients in $\mathrm{GSp}(4)$, and the symmetric cube correspondence carries $\mathrm{GL}(2)$ cusp forms to $\mathrm{GL}(4)$. In the holomorphic setting considered here, these two constructions meet inside $\mathrm{GSp}(4)$. We prove averaged decay for the resulting class group periods over imaginary quadratic fields, expressed as averages of conditional fiber integrals. More precisely, let $f$ be a non-CM holomorphic Hecke newform with trivial central character. The mean absolute value of the associated class-group averages tends to zero along the transverse unipotent direction.

column6: Semiprime Rigidity and Growth along Powers in Integer-Sided Cyclic Polygons
column7: For a positive integer $n$, let $a(n)$ be the largest number of sides of a simple cyclic polygon of circumradius $n$ whose side lengths are positive integers. For primes $p,q$ we show that $a(pq)\in\{6,8,18\}$ and characterize each value by conditions on Gaussian and Eisenstein integers. For every integer $N\ge2$, on the other hand, $a(N^e)\to\infty$ and $\limsup_{e\to\infty}a(N^e)/e\ge2\sqrt2$; a quadratic chord tower combined with Farey neighbors gives explicit polygons, for instance $a(8192)\ge38$. We also show that an odd-sided polygon of radius $n$ exists if and only if $n$ has a prime divisor congruent to $1\pmod4$, and that $a(n)$ is even whenever at most one distinct prime divisor of $n$ is congruent to $1\pmod4$; it is also even when the Gaussian part of $n$ is the product of two distinct primes congruent to $1\pmod4$. Moreover, $a(N^e)=O_N(e^{ω(N)})$ for every fixed $N\ge2$, and $a(q^e)=Θ(e)$ for primes $q\equiv1\pmod4$; exceptional semiprime extremisers have unique side-length multisets. The proofs use a splitting lemma for angle relations by squarefree class, arithmetic in imaginary quadratic fields, bounded zero-sum problems, and a one-dimensional Farey argument. No computer-assisted step is used.

column5: Zikang Dong; Qiyu Yang; Shengbo Zhao; Guang-Liang Zhou
column6: Extreme values of derivatives of Dedekind zeta functions on the $1$-line
column7: In this paper, we establish lower bounds for extreme values of derivatives of Dedekind zeta functions on the \(1\)-line over arbitrary fixed number fields. Our result extends Yang's corresponding estimate for the Riemann zeta function in 2024, with the leading constant involving residues of Dedekind zeta functions and a moment of the Dickman function. A key ingredient is a uniform asymptotic formula for weighted friable sums involving the coefficients of Dedekind zeta functions.

column6: Multiplicity one for a linear spherical pair and its unitary analogue
column7: We prove multiplicity one for a linear spherical pair associated with $\mathrm{GL}_4(F)\times\mathrm{GL}_2(F)$ and its unitary similitude analogue associated with $\mathrm{GU}(2,2)(F)\times\mathrm{GU}(1,1)(F)$. Both results hold for all irreducible admissible representations over non-Archimedean local fields of characteristic zero. Generalized Harish-Chandra descent reduces the proofs to the analysis of closed orbits and their normal representations. The unitary proof combines reductions to the linear case with a rational classification of closed orbits and a separate analysis of the remaining normal representations. We also establish multiplicity one for unitary Shalika periods of $\mathrm{GU}(2,2)(F)$ with arbitrary irreducible admissible coefficients. A theta-period identity relates these periods to the unitary spherical pair. By varying the splitting character, we prove that every irreducible admissible representation of $\mathrm{GU}(2,2)(F)$ occurs as a quotient of a suitable big theta lift, allowing the multiplicity-one bound to pass to the Shalika periods. The linear argument also recovers Rallis's multiplicity-one theorem for twisted Jacquet modules of $\mathrm{GL}_4(F)$.

column5: Usha K. Sangale; Priyanka R. Satpute
column6: On the Diophantine equation $Cx^2+p^{2m}=y^q$
column7: We classify the primitive positive solutions of $Cx^2+p^{2m}=y^q$ under the hypotheses that $C>3$ is odd and square-free, $p,q$ are odd primes, $p\nmid C$, $q\nmid h(-C)$, and $y$ is odd. The solutions form six explicit families: one for arbitrary $q$ and five exceptional families with $q=3$, three of which arise from half-integral elements when $C\equiv3\pmod8$. The proof combines ideal factorization with Lehmer sequences and shows that representations with second coordinate $v=p^r$, $r>0$, contribute only when $q=3$.

column6: Explicit permutations of $(\mathbb{Z}/4\mathbb{Z})^m$ with uniformly bounded differential uniformity
column7: Symmetric primitives over Galois rings need nonlinear components whose differentials with respect to ring addition are controlled. Let $R=\mathrm{GR}(4,m)$ and $q=2^m$, so that $(R,+)\cong(\mathbb{Z}/4\mathbb{Z})^m$ has order $N=q^2$. For every $m\ge1$ we construct an explicit permutation $G_c$ of $R$ all of whose differentials with a nonzero input difference have probability at most $36/N$, whereas every permutation polynomial of $R$ has such a differential of probability at least $2/\sqrt{N}$ (Ronjom--Sandrib). The bound holds for the fixed permutation itself, not on average over keys. Equivalently, $Δ(G_c)\le36$ against $Δ\ge2\sqrt{N}$ for permutation polynomials; since every permutation has $Δ\ge2$, the least differential uniformity of a permutation of $(\mathbb{Z}/4\mathbb{Z})^m$ lies between $2$ and $36$ for every $m$. In Teichmuller digits $(a,b)\in\mathbb{F}_q^2$ and for $c\in\mathbb{F}_q$ of absolute trace $1$, $G_c(a,b)=(L,(L^2+L+c)a)$ with $L=(a^2+a+c)b$. The map is $F_c\circ J\circ F_c$, where $F_c(a,b)=(a,(a^2+a+c)b)$ is induced by a polynomial over $R$ and $J$ exchanges the digits: a single digit exchange between two polynomial layers yields a bound independent of $m$. The proof reduces the difference equations, in each of three types of directions, to one-variable polynomials whose degrees do not depend on $m$. For general maps $F\circ J\circ F$ with $F(a,b)=(p(a),h(a)+d(a)b)$, where $p,d,h$ have degrees bounded independently of $m$, $p'\ne0$ and $d$ has no zeros, a Jacobian identity in characteristic $2$ bounds the differentials with nonzero low input and output differences independently of $m$; the remaining directions need a separate argument, which we give for an explicit family ($Δ\le440$, resp. $510$, for odd $m$).

column6: A normalization issue in a transmitted form of Bloch's diamond formula: anti-invariant subgroup versus regulator quotient
column7: Bloch's regulator formula for an elliptic curve is often quoted with a generator of the anti-invariant subgroup $H_1(E,\mathbb{Z})^-$ and coefficient $1$ in front of the elliptic dilogarithm of the diamond product. We compare this wording with Brunault's published intersection-product formula. The natural map from the anti-invariant subgroup to the regulator quotient $H_1(E,\mathbb{Z})/H_1(E,\mathbb{Z})^+$ has index $1$ when $E(\mathbb{R})$ has two components and index $2$ when it has one. Thus, up to orientation, the coefficient is $1$ for a quotient generator and $ι(E)\in\{1,2\}$ for a subgroup generator. This is an elementary consequence of the published formula, not a new regulator theorem. We illustrate the distinction on 11.a3 using an externally proved regulator anchor and the Brunault--Bertin special values, and on 20.a4 by high-precision numerical integration. We also correct our earlier quotation of Touafek: his printed identity is $πr=D_E((f)\diamond(g))$, with $r=(2π)^{-1}\int_{γ^-}η$. It is compatible with the subgroup normalization when $Δ<0$; when $Δ>0$ the corresponding coefficient is $1/2$, up to orientation. We do not reassess his isogeny theorem or his final exotic relation here. No new proof of Boyd's conductor-11 split-integral identity is included.

column6: Summing over Seifert Manifolds in Narain Ensemble Averages
column7: The ensemble average of Narain conformal field theories over their moduli space is a real-analytic Eisenstein series, whose Poincaré expansion can be interpreted as a sum over lens spaces weighted by the partition functions of Abelian Chern-Simons theory. In this paper we extend this correspondence from lens spaces to Seifert manifolds, which gives an example of a restricted sum over topologies of the kind that arises in three-dimensional quantum gravity. A Seifert manifold is obtained from a fixed core, a punctured surface times a circle, by gluing solid tori to its boundary tori, and we place a copy of the Narain theory on each of these tori. The ensemble average supplies the sum over the solid tori, or more precisely over marked presentations with fixed base genus, number of fibers and integer Seifert invariant. The resulting sum converges absolutely and is a polynomial in the components of the vector-valued Eisenstein series. When all the boundary tori share a single modulus, the average acquires connected corrections, which we identify with wormholes gluing the core to itself; for two boundary tori, the terms with rational Lagrangian sublattices of the Siegel-Eisenstein series are realized by wormholes containing an exceptional fiber. After reduction along the fiber, the construction closely parallels the two-dimensional topological gravity of Marolf and Maxfield, with the base of the fibration playing the role of their spacetime. We also discuss Dehn fillings of 3-manifolds with torus boundary, non-orientable bases, and the surgery formula. Our results suggest that modularity could be an organizing principle in the summation of geometries in quantum gravity.

column5: Ho Yun Jung; Ja Kyung Koo; Dong Hwa Shin
column6: On the Hasse-Sugawara problem and its application to Hilbert's twelfth problem
column7: We give an analytic proof of the Hasse-Sugawara problem by treating the seven remaining families of moduli. We also construct an explicit integer translate of a Weber value whose relative norms generate every intermediate field, and express these generators using extended form class groups.

column6: Reducible fibers of polynomials over integers: the Hilbert-Siegel problem over $\mathbb{Q}$ and its applications
column7: Given a polynomial $f\in \mathbb{Q}[X]$, the Hilbert--Siegel problem asks for a description of the set of all values $t_0\in \mathbb{Z}$, possibly up to a finite set, such that $f(X)-t_0$ is reducible. Reducibility occurs trivially for $t_0$ in the value set of some non-linear left-composition factor of $f$. The problem therefore reduces to determining the polynomials having infinitely many further reducible values. The biggest step towards a solution so far was taken in joint work of the author with Behajaina and Neftin. We strengthen some of the methods obtained in that work to present the complete solution of the Hilbert--Siegel problem over $\mathbb{Q}$. We give applications to the problem of newly reducible iterates of polynomials, and to an unlikely intersection problem on simultaneous reducible fibers of two polynomial maps over $\mathbb{Q}$, generalizing a result by Bilu and Tichy.

column6: Calogero-Moser Polynomial Approximations and Dwork Congruences for Complete Flags
column7: We construct $p$-adic polynomial approximations to the zero-framing cohomological quasimap vertex of cotangent bundles to complete flag varieties from the trigonometric Calogero--Moser system. Negative integer couplings give regular staircase Jack polynomials with nonnegative integer coefficients. We compare them with complete-flag master polynomials extending the construction of Smirnov--Varchenko. Both families converge coefficientwise to the vertex and satisfy the full commuting equations modulo $p^s$. For $n\geq3$, we prove sharp degree-dependent congruences and compute leading residues at every $p$-power scale. Their discrepancy has coefficient norm $p^{-1}$ and an exact weighted Gauss norm giving uniform decay on smaller closed polydiscs. For the master family, multivariable Dwork congruences reconstruct the vertex by an infinite product. The results hold in every rank for $0<r/d\leq1/2$ and odd prime $p$.

column6: A Global Generic Locus for Elementary Abelian p-covers of P^1 with two Ramification Points
column7: In this paper, we study elementary abelian $p$-covers of $P^1$ totally ramified at exactly two points and unramified elsewhere. Such covers are isomorphic to the rank-$\ell$ Artin--Schreier curves $ X_{f, \ell} : y^{p^\ell} - y = f(x), $ where $f \in \bar{F}_p[x^{\pm 1}]$ has a pole of order $d_1>0$ at $0$ and order $d_2>0$ at $\infty$. After fixing $d_1$ and $d_2$, the cover $X_{f, \ell}$ is generic if its Newton polygon is minimal as $f$ varies over all Laurent polynomials with pole orders $d_1$ and $d_2$. For $p$ sufficiently large relative to $d_1$ and $d_2$, we construct a combinatorial cost polygon $GL(d_1,d_2,p)$ and prove that its attainment is characterized by the nonvanishing of a homogeneous polynomial in the coefficients of $f$. Moreover, we prove that these conditions stabilize: there exists a Zariski-open dense subset $U$ in the coefficient space that is defined over $\Q$ and depends only on $d_1$ and $d_2$, whereby for any $f$ whose coefficients lie in $U(\overline{\Q})$, the reduction is generic at every prime ideal above sufficiently large rational primes, and for every rank $\ell$ permitted by the residue field. This result extends Zhu's result for one ramification point.

column6: Infinitely many negative terms in two weighted partition sequences
column7: Recently, Andrews and El Bachraoui introduced partition-counting functions $a_2(n)$ and $b_2(n)$, together with their signed analogues $a'_2(n)$ and $b'_2(n)$, and proved that $a'_2(n), b'_2(n)>0$ for all $n\geq 3$. For $m\geq 2$, the latter functions extend naturally to $a'_m(n)$ and $b'_m(n)$, defined by \begin{align*} \sum_{n\geq 0} a'_m(n)q^n &= -\frac{q}{1-q} \frac{(q^m;q^m)_\infty}{(q;q^m)_\infty} +\frac{q}{(1-q)^2},\\ \sum_{n\geq 0} b'_m(n)q^n &= -\frac{q(1-q^{m-1})}{1-q} \frac{(q^{2m};q^m)_\infty}{(q;q^m)_\infty} +\frac{q}{1-q} \left( \frac{1}{1-q} -\frac{q^{m-1}}{1-q^{m+1}} \right). \end{align*} They asked whether there exists an integer $m>2$ for which $a'_m(n)$ is eventually positive, and posed the same question for $b'_m(n)$. In this paper, we resolve these two questions.

column6: On the Space Defined by the Modular Transformation Law for Multiple Eisenstein Series
column7: Motivated by a modular transformation law for multiple Eisenstein series established by Yu, we introduce spaces of holomorphic functions satisfying this law together with an additional filtration condition. We show that these spaces contain the spaces spanned by admissible multiple Eisenstein series, are finitedimensional in each weight, and share several structural properties with them. We also obtain an explicit formula for the generating function of their dimensions. However, the inclusions are known to be strict for certain weights. Thus, the defining conditions do not suffice to characterize the spaces spanned by admissible multiple Eisenstein series.

column6: The module structure of ideals in degree $p$ extensions of $p$-adic fields
column7: Let $L/K$ be a degree $p$ extension of $p$-adic fields. We shall provide a complete characterization for the freeness of any fractional ideal $\mathfrak{p}_L^h$, $h\in\mathbb{Z}$, of $L$ as a module over its associated order $\mathfrak{A}_{L/K}(h)$ in the only Hopf-Galois structure on $L/K$, and an explicit description of $\mathfrak{A}_{L/K}(h)$. We show that there is no loss of generality in assuming that $0\leq h\leq p-1$ and that the normal closure of $L/K$ is totally ramified over $K$. If $L/K$ is maximally ramified, then $\mathfrak{A}_{L/K}(h)$ is the maximal $\mathcal{O}_K$-order in $H$ and $\mathfrak{p}_L^h$ is $\mathfrak{A}_{L/K}(h)$-free. The remaining cases correspond to typical extensions. For these, we provide an $\mathcal{O}_K$-basis of $\mathfrak{A}_{L/K}(h)$ and a characterization for the condition that $\mathfrak{p}_L^h$ is $\mathfrak{A}_{L/K}(h)$-free. In the non-exceptional cases, which had been partially studied in the Galois setting, the characterization depends on $h$ and the continued fraction expansion of $\frac{a}{p}$, where $a$ is the residue class mod $p$ of the (fractional) ramification jump $\ell$ of $L/K$. In the remaining exceptional case, where $L/K$ is almost maximally ramified and $a+1\leq h\leq p-1$, it consists in a numerical common minimizer condition.

column6: On the exponential Diophantine equation $\left(P_{n+1}^{(k)}\right)^{x}-\left(P_{n-1}^{(k)}\right)^{x}=2P_{m}^{(k)}$
column7: For the Pell numbers one has $P_{n+1}-P_{n-1}=2P_n$ and $P_{n+1}^2-P_{n-1}^2=2P_{2n}$. We look for all the solutions of $\big(P_{n+1}^{(k)}\big)^x-\big(P_{n-1}^{(k)}\big)^x=2P_m^{(k)}$ in positive integers $k\ge2$, $n$, $m$, $x$, where $P^{(k)}$ is the $k$-generalized Pell sequence. We prove that for $k=2$ the two identities above give all the solutions, and that for $k\ge3$ the only solutions are $(n,m,x)=(1,1,1),(1,2,2),(2,2,1)$. In contrast with the analogous equation for $k$-generalized Fibonacci numbers, there are no parametric families of solutions. The proof uses an auxiliary equation with Fibonacci numbers which does not depend on $k$, Matveev's lower bound for linear forms in logarithms, the reduction of Dujella and Pethő, and, for large $k$, the fact that the dominant root of $P^{(k)}$ is very close to $\varphi^2$.

column6: On the exponential Diophantine equation $\left(P_{n}^{(k)}\right)^{x}+\left(P_{r}^{(k)}\right)^{x}=P_{m}^{(k)}$
column7: The Pell numbers satisfy $P_n^2+P_{n+1}^2=P_{2n+1}$, and Bravo, Luca and Pomeo recently found all the cases in which the sum of the $x$-th powers of two consecutive $k$-generalized Pell numbers is again a $k$-generalized Pell number. We ask what happens when the two indices are arbitrary, that is, we solve $\big(P_n^{(k)}\big)^x+\big(P_r^{(k)}\big)^x=P_m^{(k)}$ in positive integers $k\ge2$, $n\ge r$, $m$ and $x$. The answer is that nothing new appears: apart from $1^x+1^x=2$, every solution has consecutive indices. The proof combines linear forms in logarithms with an auxiliary Fibonacci equation which does not depend on $k$, and, for large $k$, with the fact that the dominant root of the sequence is very close to $\varphi^2$. For the reduction step, the method of Dujella and Pethő fails for large indices and has to be replaced by a criterion of Legendre type.

column6: Deterministic Polynomial-Time Primality Testing with a Single Binomial Congruence
column7: We give a deterministic polynomial-time primality test whose main verification is the congruence $(1+X)^n=1+X^n$ in $C_n[X]/(X^r-b(Y))$, where $C_n=(\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z})[Y]/(Φ_r(Y))$. Two identities in the coefficient ring normalize $b$ and ensure compatibility with the main congruence. A finite-field root count and a lattice bound show that an accepted input is a prime power; elementary preprocessing excludes nontrivial perfect powers. We construct $b$ deterministically using Jacobi sums and the uniform Dedekind-zeta zero-free theorem of Cureton and Thorner, which extends OpenAI's Hecke zero-free theorem. The total bit complexity is $L^{32+o(1)}$, where $L=\lceil\log_2 n\rceil$, and verification after constructing $b$ costs $L^{6+o(1)}$. More generally, for a fixed real algebraic $1/2\leθ<1$, a common zero-free boundary $\Re s>θ$ for the relevant Dedekind zeta functions gives $L^{\max\{6,(1-θ)^{-1}\}+o(1)}$. This bound reaches $L^{6+o(1)}$ at $θ=5/6$, and hence under GRH. We state a fixed-base modification of Agrawal's conjecture for odd integers passing the base-$2$ Fermat test, using the modulus $X^r-2$ with $r$ the least positive integer not dividing $n(n-1)$.

column6: On the probability that the integer parts of polynomials are coprime
column7: We prove that for any $s\ge 2$ and polynomials $f_{1}(x),\dots,f_{s-1}(x)\in \mathbb{R}[x]$ satisfying a certain equidistribution condition, the natural density of the numbers $n\in \mathbb{N}$ such that $n,\lfloor f_{1}(n)\rfloor,\dots,\lfloor f_{s-1}(n)\rfloor$ are mutually coprime is $1/ζ(s)$. This generalises a recent result of Champagne, in which this was proven under the assumption that $f_{1}$ is linear.

column6: A converse theorem for GL(2) over global fields without root numbers
column7: We prove a converse theorem for GL(2) over global fields in which the root numbers in the twisted functional equations need not be prescribed. Instead, we allow nonzero scalar factors that are invariant under unramified twists. We show that these scalars are independent of the twisting character and obtain a unique isobaric automorphic representation with the prescribed unramified local components.

column5: Cristina Benea; Frédéric Bernicot; Victor Lie
column6: On a hybrid trilinear Hilbert transform
column7: In this paper we study the boundedness properties of a \emph{hybrid} trilinear Hilbert transform characterized by a \emph{dual regime} which simultaneously exhibits 1) \emph{resonant} (zero curvature) features, \emph{i.e.}, modulation invariance properties, and 2) \emph{non-resonant} (non-zero curvature) features. Specifically, given $a\in(0,\infty)\setminus \{1,2\}$ and $\vecλ:=(λ_1,λ_2,λ_3,λ_4)\in (\mathbb{R}\setminus\{0\})^4$ with $λ_1\neq λ_2$ and $λ_3\neq λ_4$, we provide wide-range $L^p$ bounds for the trilinear operator $$ HTHT^a_{\vecλ} (f_1,f_2,f_3)(x):= p.v. \int_{\mathbb R} f_1(x-λ_1 t)\,f_2(x-λ_2 t-λ_3 t^a)\,f_3(x-λ_4 t^a)\,\frac{dt}{t},\quad x \in \mathbb{R}\,.$$ By combining variable multiresolution, multiscale wave-packet analysis, and Rank II LGC method, our present work establishes a common framework where the diverse methodologies of all of the following naturally converge: i) the maximal truncated bilinear Hilbert transform, ii) the Biest operator, iii) the hybrid bilinear Hilbert-Carleson operator, and iv) the non-resonant (curved) trilinear Hilbert transform. Ultimately, this work reveals that the hybrid trilinear transform sits on a critical intermediate scale between the purely non-resonant case and the purely resonant regime -- the latter remaining a challenging, major (open) problem in harmonic analysis.

column6: Functoriality probes over number fields by mixed zero correlations
column7: We use an automorphic L-function over one number field as a probe for the functorial structure of another automorphic L-function over a possibly different field. No automorphic induction is assumed. We first determine the mixed Euler factors arising from the explicit formula, including the residue-degree multiplicities that occur when local traces are grouped by absolute norm. This local analysis gives four probe constructions. Rational-field probes with known base change detect constituent multiplicities and, in equal rank, exact Satake equalities. Probes over a common Galois field detect conjugacy and stabilizers. Dirichlet-character probes give congruence-weighted combinations of Satake traces even when the leading overlap vanishes. A tensor-product construction realizes general different-field probes whenever the required base changes exist. We then separate the pair calculation from the higher connected calculations and work out the cubic and quartic arithmetic explicitly. In an explicit small Fourier box these expressions yield all finite secondary orders of the centered statistics; the required pair prime number theorems also give raw and distinct-index correlations. The main analytic tools are an independent fixed-data proof of Hypothesis H over number fields, a positive-margin estimate for rationally grouped coefficients, and the theorem of Harcos-Thorner for the realized Rankin-Selberg factors. This expanded version includes the full computations, local examples, and an appendix explaining the character-extension issue avoided by the proof of Hypothesis H. The resulting probes give concrete tests of functorial relationships, while recovery of automorphic induction remains a longer-term goal.

column6: Probing automorphic induction through zero correlations and secondary arithmetic terms
column7: Zero correlations offer a way to test the cuspidal structure of an automorphic L-function, but their leading self statistics retain only coarse degree and multiplicity data. We therefore adjoin a specified cuspidal L-function as a probe and study the resulting raw mixed correlations. Assuming a factorization into cuspidal L-functions over Q, we show that a mixed pair statistic detects the probe's occurrence and recovers its multiplicity. A suitable Gevrey-order-two test eliminates the smooth-density terms and gives a subexponential error. For arbitrary smooth plateau tests, the prime number theorem of Harcos and Thorner gives an error smaller than every fixed inverse power of log T, without a self-contragredience assumption. The stronger prime number theorem of Liu and Ye gives a subexponential remainder under its stated structural assumptions, with the possible norm-twist terms made explicit. To obtain arithmetic information beyond this overlap, we compute the correlation expansion at every fixed level and inverse-logarithmic order within the original strict small-support range. We treat the pair and higher correlations separately, using Jiang's rational-field fixed-data estimates to justify the required prime-power convergence. The pair calculation identifies the mixed arithmetic finite parts and gives detailed error estimates, including the contribution of norm twists. The higher-level calculation retains connected prime-power invariants, whose first cubic contribution appears at order (log T)^{-3}. Explicit third- and fourth-level formulas and examples explain the arithmetic content of these coefficients and the limitations of self-correlations. Varying powers of the probe separates their mixed components. These formulas, together with the distinct-index sieve, provide a collection of arithmetic probe responses toward the further problem of recovering automorphic induction structure.

column6: A Korselt Characterization of Carmichael Numbers of the Form $(aC_n+1)(aC_{n+1}+1)(aC_{n+2}+1)$
column7: We study products \[ N=(aC_n+1)(aC_{n+1}+1)(aC_{n+2}+1), \] where $(C_n)$ is the Lucas--balancing sequence. Under the assumption that all three factors are prime, we give a necessary and sufficient condition for $N$ to be a Carmichael number: this happens precisely when $n$ is even and $a=kC_{n+1}$ for a positive integer $k$ satisfying \[ 48k\equiv 7\pmod{C_nC_{n+2}}. \] We derive further congruence restrictions, an explicit parametrization of the integer solutions of the resulting congruence, a lower bound for $k$, and a divisibility relation involving the middle prime factor. The characterization is conditional on the primality of the three factors and does not assert that such prime triples exist for infinitely many parameters.

column6: The signed error-sum function of tent-map expansions
column7: In this paper, we study the signed error-sum function of tent map base series introduced by Dai and Tang in 2011. We show that the function is discontinuous at every dyadic rational in the open unit interval, although it was asserted to be continuous. We determine its values at these points and analyze its range, differentiability, and variation. We also obtain sharp covering estimates for its graph and calculate the Hausdorff, box-counting, and covering dimensions of the graph, which are $1$, $1$, and $0$, respectively. Moreover, we show that the signed error sum agrees with Lévy's function away from dyadic rationals and that the unsigned error sum is the Takagi function.

column6: Convergence in law of the maximum of the Riemann zeta function on expanding intervals near the critical line
column7: Let $T \to \infty$, let $τ$ be uniformly distributed on $[T,2T]$, and let $σ= σ(T)$ be a deterministic real part approaching $1/2$ from the right. We establish the convergence in law of the recentered maximum of $\log|ζ(σ+ \mathrm{i}τ+ \mathrm{i} h)|$ over $I_θ = \smash{[ - (\log T)^θ,(\log T)^θ]}$, for every fixed $θ> 0$. Under explicit conditions on the displacement $σ- 1/2$, the recentered maximum converges to a Gumbel distribution with scale parameter $1/(2\sqrt{1 + θ})$. The recentering is an exact upper quantile of the one-point law of the associated Haar field $F_{h}^{\mathrm{H}} = \Re\sum_{p^{j}\leq X}U_{p}^{j}/(jp^{j(σ+ \mathrm{i} h)})$, where the $U_{p}$ are independent and uniformly distributed on the complex unit circle. The positive constant in the limiting distribution is characterized by a Gaussian process describing the limiting microscopic increments of the Haar field around a high point. The result is established without the Riemann hypothesis.

column6: Infinite Generalized Sidon Sets with a Negative Answer to a Problem of Szemerédi
column7: We construct infinite $B_h$ sets that repeatedly attain the density scale of finite $B_h$ sets. For every integer $h\geq2$ and every finite $B_h$ set $F$ of positive integers, we obtain an infinite $B_h$ set $A\supseteq F$ such that $$ \limsup_{x\to\infty}\frac{A(x)}{x^{1/h}}=\frac1h, \qquad \liminf_{x\to\infty}\frac{A(x)}{x^{1/h}}=0. $$ The key is to preserve density while preventing additive relations between successive blocks. A positional encoding of the finite-field moment curve has $q$ elements in an interval of length $O_h(q^h)$, while, for each $1\leq r<h$, sums arising from distinct $r$-element multisets are separated by more than $q$. This separation allows whole blocks to be appended to a prescribed finite set without a further dilation. In particular, our result gives a negative answer to a problem posed by Szemerédi \cite{szemeredi}.

column6: Finite Cotangent Power Sums Weighted by Additive Characters With Application to Mean Values of Additive-and-Multiplicatively Twisted $L$-Functions
column7: We derive explicit formulas for finite sums of powers of cotangents, both at rational and arbitrary arguments, together with their alternating counterparts, weighted by additive characters. Our method relies on Apostol--Bernoulli polynomials and on the partial fraction expansion of trigonometric functions. As applications, we solve the problem posed by Berndt, Kim and Zaharescu \cite{BKZ:2023} on evaluating $\sum\csc^{2m}$ and $\sum\sec^{2m}$ at rational arguments, recover as a special case the classical Berndt--Yeap formula, and relate our identities to spectral zeta functions of circulant graphs. Furthermore, to systematically evaluate higher-order derivatives arising from the Lipschitz summation formula, we introduce a novel sequence of polynomial coefficients $c_{m,j}(β)$, termed \emph{deformed cotangent coefficients}, and establish their recursive and algebraic properties. Using these coefficients, we establish a general additive-and-multiplicatively twisted character mean value theorem for Lerch zeta functions, significantly extending the framework of Bayad and Raouj to incorporate additive character twists.

column6: Groups of Prime Units
column7: We study groups of units modulo $n$ whose nonidentity elements are all primes in $\{1,\ldots,n-1\}$. We prove that there are only nine groups of prime units which are the full group of units modulo $n$, and there are fewer than $10^{22}$ groups of prime units containing all prime units in the possible range $(\sqrt n,n-\sqrt n)\cup\{n-1\}$. We prove under Dickson's conjecture that there are infinitely many groups of prime units of arbitrary order $d \ge 2$ modulo composite integers. We prove under Schinzel's Hypothesis H that there are infinitely many groups of prime units of order 3 modulo a prime $r$. We prove that the number of such prime moduli $r$ smaller than $X$ is $\ll X/(\log X)^3$.

column5: Qian Li; Bo Tan; Qing-Long Zhou
column6: Inhomogeneous Fiber Refinement of Gallagher's Theorem
column7: Let \(s>0\), \(α,γ\in\mathbb{R}\), and let \(ψ\colon \mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{R}_{>0}\) be a non-increasing function. Consider the limsup set \[ W_s(ψ,α,γ) = \left\{ β\in[0,1] \colon \norm{nβ-γ} < \frac{ψ(n)}{\norm{nα}^{\,s}} \ \text{ for infinitely many } n\in\mathbb{N} \right\}. \] Chow [Duke J. Math. 2018] settled the measure-theoretic result for \(s=1\). In this paper, we investigate the Lebesgue measure of \(W_s(ψ,α,γ)\) for general \(s>0\).

column6: Irrationality measures for $Γ(1/4)$ and $Γ(1/3)$
column7: Let $μ$ denote the irrationality exponent. Bruiltet proved in 2002 that $μ(Γ(1/4))\le 10^{143}$ and $μ(Γ(1/3))\le 10^{151}$. We prove $μ(Γ(1/4))\le 3.24\cdot 10^{26}$ and $μ(Γ(1/3))\le 1.74\cdot 10^{26}$, with explicit thresholds $h(p/q)\ge 5.4\cdot 10^{7}$ and $h(p/q)\ge 4.7\cdot 10^{7}$ respectively, against $10^{75}$ and $10^{79}$ in the published statements. The proof keeps the architecture of Bruiltet's argument -- Philippon's transcendence criterion together with a zero estimate in commutative algebraic groups -- and replaces three of its ingredients. First, an approximate Schwarz principle based on Hermite interpolation replaces the gravitation estimate of Reyssat; on a lattice point set its cost per node is governed by a lattice energy and drops from about 3.7 to about 1.0. Second, a summation lemma for the failure of Diaz's approximation lemma sharpens the passage from an approximation measure to an irrationality measure. Third, the auxiliary point is taken at a torsion point of order 4, respectively 3, which lowers the degree of the base field from 8d to 2d. All numerical constants are produced by a verifier run in interval arithmetic, supplied as ancillary files.

column6: A new upper bound for the irrationality exponent of $ζ(5)$
column7: Fauzan's determinantal proof that $ζ(5)$ is irrational also yields $|ζ(5)-a/b|>b^{-260}$ for all large $b$. The exponent is the product $\varrhoλ/\varepsilon$ of three constants attached to the construction, of which $\varrho$ governs the growth of a relative matrix norm. We show that $\varrho$ may be taken to be $9.09$ instead of $6933/500=13.866$, and deduce $|ζ(5)-a/b|>b^{-171}$ for all integers $a$ and all sufficiently large integers $b$, so that the irrationality exponent of $ζ(5)$ is at most $171$. Two closed-form functions replace two worst-case estimates: a node function, which bounds the residue weights individually instead of uniformly, and the external field of the energy estimate, which replaces a factor-by-factor bound on the weight. The result is conditional on Fauzan's preprint. An exact arithmetic verifier is attached.

column6: Counting Nilpotent Galois extensions with prescribed genus number
column7: Let $G$ be a nontrivial finite nilpotent group. In this paper, we study the distribution of genus numbers of Galois extensions of $\Q$ with Galois group isomorphic to $G$, ordered by absolute discriminant. We show that the proportion of fields with any prescribed genus number tends to zero, and obtain a quantitative bound for this proportion. Moreover, if every element of order $\ell$ in $G$ is central, where $\ell$ is the smallest prime divisor of $|G|$, we determine the orders of magnitude of the average genus number and its higher moments.

column6: Smooth numbers in simultaneous arithmetic progressions
column7: We prove a mean value theorem on the distribution of smooth numbers in two simultaneous arithmetic progressions, with generalizing a result of Drappeau. Let $\varepsilon>0$ and $(\log x)^C<y<x^{1/C}$ for a sufficiently large $C$. Our result implies that $y$-smooth numbers are well-distributed in the residue classes of a fixed integer $a$ on average over moduli $\leq x^{5/9-\varepsilon}$ and $\leq x^{153/256-\varepsilon}$ for each $|a|\leq x$, which improves Drappeau's range $\leq x^{6/11-\varepsilon}$. As an application, we show that a positive proportion of $y$-smooth numbers $n\leq x$ satisfy $\min(P^+(n-1), P^+(n+1))>x^{407/720}$.

column6: A Counterexample to Wooley's $L^1$ Question for Beatty Sequences
column7: For real numbers $α$ and $β$, let $\mathcal{B}(α,β)=\{\lfloorαm+β\rfloor:m\in\mathbb{N}\}$. Wooley asked whether the exponential sum over $\mathcal{B}(α,β)\cap[1,N]$ always has $L^1$ norm $O_{α,β}(\log N)$. We give a negative answer. We construct fixed $α>1$ and $β$, with $1/α$ of finite Diophantine type, such that the $L^1$ norm is $\gg(\log N)^2$ for infinitely many $N$. Wooley also proved that this $L^1$ norm is $O_{α,β}((\log(2N))^2)$ when $1/α$ has finite Diophantine type. Our example shows that his upper bound is sharp.

column6: A solution to the Erdős-Sárközy product-density problem
column7: Color each positive integer red or blue, and call an integer a same-color product if it is the product of two red numbers or of two blue numbers. Does there exist a universal constant $c > 0$ such that: For each fixed coloring, and for all sufficiently large $M$ (where "sufficiently large" may depend on the coloring), at least $cM$ of the integers among $1$, $2$, $\ldots$, $M$ are same-colored products (allowing for equal factors, and where each distinct product is counted once)? This problem was given (in an equivalent way) in Guy's famous text on unsolved problems in number theory, and was posed (in equivalent ways) by Erdős and Sárközy in 1990, in the proceedings of the 1988 Banff number theory conference, and 1993 [Colloq. Math.], and this problem seems to have remained open. We succeed in solving this problem, by proving that no such universal constant exists.

column6: Adelic Galois representations are maximal for almost all Drinfeld modules
column7: Let $r\geq 3$ be an integer, let $q$ be an odd prime power, and set $A=\mathbb{F}_q[T]$ and $F=\mathbb{F}_q(T)$. We study the Galois representations associated with rank $r$ Drinfeld modules of the form $φ_T=T+g_1τ+\cdots+g_rτ^r$, where $g_i\in A$ and $g_r\neq 0$. Ordering the coefficient tuples $\vec{g}=(g_1,\ldots,g_r)$ by their maximum degree, we prove that, for a density-one set of tuples, the $λ$-adic Galois representation is surjective for every prime $λ$ of $A$, and the adelic Galois image contains $\mathrm{SL}_r(\widehat A)$. Moreover, for every tuple in this set, the index of the adelic image equals the index of the corresponding rank-one determinant representation and hence divides $q-1$. These results extend Zywina's theorem in rank $2$ to arbitrary ranks $r\geq 3$. As a further consequence, we establish the existence of rank $r$ Drinfeld modules with surjective adelic Galois representations for every $r\geq 3$, extending previous existence results which were known for prime values of $r$.

column6: An Odd-Arch Family of Perturbed Hofstadter Q-Recursions: Gaussian Profiles and Exact Frequency Laws
column7: For every integer $p\ge2$, we construct a globally well-defined positive odd sequence $Q_p$ satisfying, after an explicit finite initial block, $Q_p(n)=Q_p(n-Q_p(n-1))+Q_p(n-Q_p(n-2))-(-1)^n$. Its binary block words admit the exact factorization $U_{p,k}=(A_k\overline{A}_{k+1})^{p-1}A_{k+2}$, producing exactly $2p-1$ alternating signed arches per natural block. The elementary word heights converge uniformly to the Gaussian isoperimetric profile $\varphi\circΦ^{-1}$. For each fixed $p$, this yields an explicit dyadic limiting profile with $2p-1$ sign transitions and a sharp relative-error constant $Λ_p=b_p/2$, where $b_p$ is determined by $b_p((3p-1)/2+Φ(-b_p))=\varphi(b_p)$. We determine all zeros and parity crossings in sufficiently large dyadic blocks. For $p\ge3$, there are exactly $2p-1$ transverse even-index zeros, whereas the three-arch case $p=2$ exhibits an alternating four/six-zero pattern. An ordered frequency factorization gives exact dyadic histograms, moments, total-variation distances, and extremal multiplicities. The limiting frequency generating function $z^3/(2-z)$ is universal, although the highest finite multiplicities depend on $p$. Finally, the summatory function has main terms $N^2/4+(N/2)\log_2N$, an explicit parameter-dependent log-periodic term of order $N$, and remainder $O_p(N/\sqrt{\log N})$.

column6: Improved first moments of primitive quartic and sextic Dirichlet $L$-functions
column7: We study the smoothed first moments of primitive quartic and sextic Dirichlet $L$-functions for which every nontrivial power of the character remains primitive. Assuming the generalized Riemann hypothesis for the Dirichlet and finite order Hecke $L$-functions occurring in the proof, we obtain asymptotic formulas with errors $O(Q^{\frac{49}{58}+\eps})$ and $O(Q^{\frac{23}{26}+\eps})$, respectively. We follow the double Dirichlet series approach of Gao and Zhao. The main ingredient is a joint estimate for the two sums arising from the removal of rational prime divisors, with the Möbius coefficients retained. This gives a quotient of Dirichlet $L$-functions. Under GRH, we bound both the Dirichlet $L$-functions and their reciprocals. Combining the joint estimate with estimates for the generating series of Gauss sums gives larger regions of meromorphic continuation. These regions do not separate the possible secondary terms.

column6: A secondary term in the first moment of primitive cubic Dirichlet L-functions
column7: P. Gao and L. Zhao obtained an asymptotic formula for the smoothed first moment of primitive cubic Dirichlet \(L\)-functions over \(\Q\) with conductors coprime to \(3\), with a main term of order \(Q\) and error \(O\left(Q^{\frac{7}{8}+\eps}\right)\) under the generalized Lindelöf hypothesis. Building on their double Dirichlet series, we assume the generalized Riemann hypothesis and separate an explicit secondary term of order \(Q^{\frac{5}{6}}\) in the same family, with error \(O\left(Q^{\frac{23}{28}+\eps}\right)\). We explicitly evaluate the secondary coefficient and prove that it is strictly negative. We also prove unconditionally that the secondary polynomial in the squarefree second moment of the natural cubic Hecke \(L\)-functions over \(\Q(\sqrt{-3})\) has degree one and strictly positive leading coefficient, which we evaluate explicitly.

column6: Topological transcendence degree and the dimension problem for perfectoid spaces
column7: Let $K$ be a perfectoid field of characteristic $p$ with countable value group (for example, $K=\mathbb{C}_{p}^{\flat}$). We study Zariski-closed subsets \begin{equation*}Z\subseteq \mathbb{B}_{K}^{n,\mathrm{perfd}}\end{equation*}of the $n$-dimensional perfectoid closed unit ball $\mathbb{B}_{K}^{n,\mathrm{perfd}}$ over $K$. We use an example of Gleason, and its generalization obtained in the authors' previous work, to show that two natural notions of dimension for such Zariski-closed subsets, the Krull dimension $\dim(Z)$ and Huber's iterated transcendence degree $\mathrm{dim.tr}(Z)$, do not coincide, and that the gap between them can be arbitrarily large.

column6: Counterexamples to uniqueness for a discrete X-ray transform under quadratic decay
column7: We show nonuniqueness for a discrete X-ray transform on $\mathbb Z^2$ under quadratic decay. We construct an explicit nonzero function in $\ell^1(\mathbb Z^2)$ with pointwise decay $O(|z|^{-2})$ whose sums over integer lines vanish. We also obtain an infinite-dimensional null space with the same decay assumption. Furthermore, we show a result which indicates that the decay rate $|z|^{-2}$ may be sharp and faster decay may imply uniqueness.

column6: Contact multiplicity and a sharp six-map bound for collinear self-similar dendrites
column7: Let $K\subset\mathbb{C}$ be the attractor of $n\ge2$ similarities $z\mapstoλz+b_k$, $0<|λ|<1$, whose fixed points are evenly spaced on a line, and suppose that $K$ does not lie in a line. We prove that $K$ can be a dendrite only if $n\le6$, and that such dendrites exist for every $2\le n\le6$; no separation or finite-intersection hypothesis is imposed. Hence, for $n\ge7$, every connected $K$ of this kind has interior points or separates the plane. Neighboring pieces of $K$ meet in similar copies of a single contact set. In a dendrite exactly one first-level piece meets this set, whereas for $n\ge7$ at least $n-\lceil2\sqrt{n-1}\rceil\ge2$ do, a bound attained by explicit quadratic parameters. The proof combines a planar translation obstruction for replicated contact arcs with an estimate based on Jensen's formula. After normalizing to $z\mapsto t+z/c$, $t\in\{-n+1,-n+3,\ldots,n-1\}$, the connectedness locus is the closure, outside the unit disk, of the roots of monic integer polynomials of height at most $n-1$. The same estimate shows that, for $n\ge7$, every such polynomial with a non-real root $c$ satisfying $|c|^2\ge\lceil2\sqrt{n-1}\rceil+1$ has subleading coefficient of absolute value at most $\lceil2\sqrt{n-1}\rceil$, and that this bound is sharp. Accordingly, for $n\ge7$, at every non-real boundary point $c$ of the locus with $|c|>1$, each expansion $c=\sum_{j\ge0}d_jc^{-j}$ with integer digits $|d_j|\le n-1$ has $|d_0|\le\lceil2\sqrt{n-1}\rceil$.

column6: Small-LCM Distinct Covering Systems via Segmented Local Search
column7: We construct distinct covering systems with minimum moduli 8, 9, 10, 11 and least common multiples 20160, 75600, 302400, 3326400, respectively, and conjecture that these values are minimal. For minimum modulus 8, the exclusion computations leave only 10080 and 15120 unresolved below our construction. The constructions use segmented local search: moduli are introduced in increasing blocks, followed by joint reoptimization of selected blocks. We give complete residue lists and an independent integer-arithmetic verifier. Two computational studies, comprising 180 initial runs and 130 follow-up runs, compare initialization orders, revisit rules and seed-bank capacities under fixed scan limits.

column6: Halving Partitions and Hyperbinary Expansions
column7: Starting from a positive integer, repeatedly halve the current value, rounding up or down. Which resulting sequences have terms that add to the starting integer? A simple balance identity turns the rounding choices into hyperbinary expansions, in which each power of two occurs at most twice. This correspondence gives exact counts by length and an injection into the expansions counted by Stern's diatomic sequence. We characterize equality in the resulting bound by the binary digits of the odd part of the integer. We also determine the unique longest partition and give a short recursive counting algorithm. When the required total is allowed to vary, the chain counts eventually equal Stern's number, and we determine the exact threshold. A direct proof shows that the counts of hyperbinary expansions in the three length classes modulo three differ by at most one. For sufficiently long halving partitions, the counts by length first weakly increase and then weakly decrease, although the full sequence need not do so.

column5: Francesco Campagna; Nathan Jones; Francesco Pappalardi; Peter Stevenhagen
column6: Entanglement for elliptic curve group orders
column7: For an elliptic curve $E$ defined over a number field $K$ and $\mathfrak{p}$ a prime of good reduction of $E/K$, we let $n_\mathfrak{p}=\#E(k_\mathfrak{p})$ be the order of the group of points over the residue class field $k_\mathfrak{p}$. Divisibility of $n_\mathfrak{p}$ by a prime $\ell$ depends on the splitting behavior of $\mathfrak{p}$ in the $\ell$-division field $K(E[\ell](\bar{K}))$ of $E$ and, generically, divisibility of $n_\mathfrak{p}$ by different primes $\ell_1$ and $\ell_2$ are `independent events' on the set of primes $\mathfrak{p}$ of good reduction. However, there do exist elliptic curves with `entangled division fields' for which infinitely many $n_\mathfrak{p}$ are coprime to $\ell_1$ and infinitely many $n_\mathfrak{p}$ are coprime to $\ell_2$, but no $n_\mathfrak{p}$ is coprime to to $\ell_1 \ell_2$. For $\ell_1=2$, we classify in group theoretical terms the entanglement giving rise to this behavior, and count up to isomorphism the number of `special $2\ell$-division groups' exhibiting the phenomenon. A final section shows how such groups may be realized as the Galois group of $2\ell$ division fields for elliptic curves $E/\mathbf{Q}$.

column6: Fermat curves and explicit class field theory for real quadratic number fields
column7: We use Fermat curves with real multiplication and classical CM theory to construct an explicit class field theory for arbitrary real quadratic number fields. The underlying strategy is well-established in computational class field theory, our main contribution is a geometric model to realize this strategy explicitly. This approach complements the recent breakthrough works solving conjectures by Brumer, Stark and Shintani and gives an alternative constructive solution to Hilbert's 12th problem for real quadratic fields.

column6: On Wagstaff primes in the $k$-Pell number sequence
column7: A Wagstaff prime is a prime number of the form $(2^{\mathfrak{p}}+1)/3$, where $\mathfrak{p}$ is an odd prime. For an integer $k\ge 2$, the sequence of $k$-generalized Pell numbers $\bigl(P_n^{(k)}\bigr)_{n\ge 2-k}$ is the linear recurrence of order $k$ given by $P_n^{(k)}=2P_{n-1}^{(k)}+P_{n-2}^{(k)}+\cdots+P_{n-k}^{(k)}$ for $n\ge 2$, with initial values $P_{2-k}^{(k)}=\cdots=P_{0}^{(k)}=0$ and $P_1^{(k)}=1$. For $k=2$ this is the classical Pell sequence. Motivated by the recent determination of the Wagstaff primes in the $k$-Fibonacci and $k$-Lucas sequences, we study the exponential Diophantine equation $P_n^{(k)}=(2^{\mathfrak{p}}+1)/3$ in positive integers $n,k$ and an odd prime $\mathfrak{p}\geq 3$, with $k\ge 2$. We show that this equation has no solutions, that is no $k$-Pell number is a Wagstaff prime. The proof combines linear forms in logarithms of algebraic numbers with reduction based on the theory of continued fractions, together with a computational verification in the remaining finite range.

column6: Uniform cubic bounds for irrational values of the dilogarithm
column7: We study explicit denominator conditions ensuring the irrationality of the dilogarithm at positive and negative rational points. We prove that $\operatorname{Li}_2(p/q)$ is irrational whenever $q>(4e^4/27)p^3$, and obtain an explicit, slightly smaller threshold for $\operatorname{Li}_2(-p/q)$. The positive argument specializes the Rhin--Viola integral family and uses a uniform estimate for a restricted prime divisor. The negative argument combines the same arithmetic construction with three adjacent integral moments and an explicit maximization. We also give finite-numerator refinements by interpolating certified partition bounds and by introducing a comparison measure with a quadratic tail. In particular, $\operatorname{Li}_2(5/q)$ is irrational for every integer $q\ge418$. The proof separates the established integral and determinant constructions from the parameter estimates and finite certificates used here.

column6: Two-point Padé approximation and patterns in continued fractions for $(F_{n+1}/F_n)^k$
column7: We explore the simple continued fraction expansion for the $k$th power of the Fibonacci convergent $F_{n+1}/F_n$, as $n$ grows. For most $k$, this continued fraction consists of $k$ linearly growing \emph{patches} of infinite periodic continued fractions separated by \emph{junctions} that vary periodically in $n$. But under special conditions, two patches merge or, more strikingly, an exponentially growing \emph{monster term} replaces two patches and the junction between them. We trace these phenomena to properties of the Padé approximants that approximate $x^k$ near $x = φ$ and $x = \barφ$ simultaneously. We prove the patterns for second-order unimodular recurrences and compute several more instances of this rare and apparently previously unnoticed monster term.

column6: The Golden Quadruple: Four Reals Whose Differences Form a Geometric Progression, Rigidity of the Golden Ratio, and a Bohr Almost Periodic Cosine Sum
column7: Let $\varphi=(1+\sqrt5)/2$. The set $\{0,\varphi,\varphi^2,\varphi^3\}$ is classical (Euclid, Elements XIII.8): by $\varphi^2=\varphi+1$ its six pairwise differences take the values $1,\varphi,\varphi^2,\varphi^3$, with multiplicities $1,2,2,1$. We write it as the golden quadruple $S=(F, F-a, F-b, F-a-b)$, $a=\varphi u$, $b=\varphi^2u$, $F>a+b$, and study its extremal and rigidity properties. No five distinct reals have all their positive differences in $\{u\varphi^n:n\in\mathbb{Z}\}$; this follows from a result of Lenstra (1977), and we give a self-contained proof. We give an elementary proof of uniqueness: every four-element set with this property is a translate of $u\varphi^m\{0,\varphi,\varphi^2,\varphi^3\}$ for some $m\in\mathbb{Z}$, and if all its differences lie in $\{u,\varphi u,\varphi^2u,\varphi^3u\}$ it is a translate of $S$. Among all $x>1$, only $x=\varphi$ admits a four-point set of reals whose set of distinct differences is $\{c,cx,cx^2,cx^3\}$. For the analogous quadruple with base $x\neq\varphi$ the failure is measured by two closure residues, which along Fibonacci quotients equal $\pm u/\mathrm{Fib}_n^2$ and $\pm \mathrm{Fib}_{n+1}u/\mathrm{Fib}_n^3$. The cosine sum $C_S(t)=\sum\cos(2πd t)$ over the six differences equals $8\cos^2(πa t)\cos^2(πb t)-2$; it is not periodic but is Bohr almost periodic, with explicit almost periods $τ_n=\mathrm{Fib}_n/u$, and we determine the two-term asymptotics $\sup_t|C_S(t+τ_n)-C_S(t)|=6\sqrt3 π\varphi^{-n}-2\sqrt3 π^3\varphi^{-3n}+O(\varphi^{-5n})$, with optimal constants; the inclusion length of the $\varepsilon$-almost periods is of order $1/\varepsilon$. For a scale $K>0$ the golden ladder $ν_n=K\varphi^{-n}$ realises the construction with differences $ν_{200},\dots,ν_{203}$; we evaluate it for $K=\sqrt{c^5/(Gh)}$. All proofs are elementary and self-contained.

column6: An exhaustion-aware product moment and zero-free half-planes for Hecke L-functions
column7: We refine the ordinary product moment in the cubic-theta comparison by allowing a returned prime product to be exhausted. The return stops either when the positive-prime length inequality holds or when the established prime-free ordinary estimate applies. Keeping the extracted central coefficients gives a local normalization inequality on a larger domain. On the critical ordinary-length interval this yields a net first-mean gain of $1/20000$. We prove the complementary-class, short-sum and algebraic comparison inequalities directly, and obtain the endpoint $B_*-1/160000=0.87446205769353\ldots$, where $B_*$ is Liu's algebraic boundary. The zero-free conclusion is conditional on the cited general-field theta, detector, prior-bound and Mellin input theorems in their stated uniform forms. The proof includes the actual return weights, both approximate-functional-equation arms, the principal-residue normalization and descent to arbitrary number fields.

column6: Stacked-bases Properties, maximal ideals and polynomial closures of Rings of Integer-Valued Polynomials
column7: We study the integer-valued polynomial ring with the stacked-bases property, maximal ideals above valuation ideals, and the polynomial closure of matrices with prescribed characteristic polynomials. A content argument gives stacked-bases properties for integer-valued polynomial rings over number-field integer rings. The construction of Hagg and Mortberg provides a Bezout domain without this property. For rank-one valuation domains, maximal ideals are described by evaluations and pseudo-convergent sequences. For matrices, we give congruence-ideal and companion-lattice criteria, together with finite-level tests to characterize the polynomial closures.

column6: The covering radius of the first-order Reed-Muller code in nine variables is 242
column7: We prove that the covering radius of the binary first-order Reed-Muller code RM(1,9) is exactly 242. Equivalently, the maximum nonlinearity of a Boolean function in nine variables is 242. Our proof combines a one-point rigidity theorem with a spectral and computational exclusion of the two larger candidate nonlinearities. We first show that every nine-variable Boolean function of nonlinearity 243 admits a unique one-point modification that raises its nonlinearity to 244: the point to be changed is the vector sum of its support. This part uses exact Walsh-update identities, integer interpolation, rigidity of a quadratic residue, and a sharp Walsh l1 estimate for cubic Boolean functions. To exclude nonlinearity 244, we use Parseval's identity and congruences of integral Walsh coefficients to force an exceptionally restricted spectrum. An associated cubic residue phase must attain the extremal Walsh l1 bound 10240. We eliminate one equality spectrum by hyperplane slicing; the other forces the original Boolean function from the signs of the cubic phase and yields a double-complement-pairing identity for its cubic top part. The classification of alternating trilinear forms over F2, an exact filter of their representatives, and two exhaustive enumerations of 218 quadratic supplements then rule out every remaining candidate. Together with the known construction attaining nonlinearity 242, these arguments establish the asserted covering radius.

column6: On Ramanujan's cubic continued fraction, II
column7: We show that all the periodic points with period $n \ge 3$ of the algebraic function defined by the relation $g(x,y) = x^2+2xy^2-y = 0$ are expressible in terms of values of Ramanujan's cubic continued fraction $c(τ)$. It is shown that the values $c(w/2), c(w/6), c(w/6+1/2)$ are periodic points, for specific elements $w$ in the order of discriminant $-d$ in $K = \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-d})$, with $-d \equiv 1$ (mod $8$); and all the periodic points are conjugates of these values or specific linear fractional expressions in their conjugates, times cube roots of unity. These periodic points are determined by relating them to the periodic points of the algebraic function defined by $k(x,y)= -xy^2+x^2+y^2+3x = 0$; and these periodic points (for periods $\ge 2$) generate ring class fields over $K$.

column6: Twisting-free converse theorems for $Γ_0(32)$ and $Γ_0(36)$
column7: We prove twisting-free converse theorems for $Γ_0(32)$ and $Γ_0(36)$ under the setting of Conrey--Farmer, namely assuming a single functional equation and a suitable Euler product, with particular shapes at ramified primes. The proofs make substantial use of the ramified primes, with methods somewhat different from the existing ones in the literature.

column5: Urtzi Buijs; José Manuel Moreno Fernández
column6: Identities for generalized Bernoulli numbers from a Lie model of the 2-disk
column7: We define generalized Bernoulli numbers as appropriate coefficients of the Baker--Campbell--Hausdorff (BCH) product formula, extending the classical sequence of rational numbers to a 2-dimensional setting. We give an identity involving these numbers and the classical Bernoulli numbers which is equivalent to the existence of a particular complete differential graded Lie algebra modelling a cell decomposition of the 2-disk and based on the Lawrence--Sullivan model of the interval. From this identity we derive explicit quadratic relations. The existence of Lie models for the symmetries of the interval and the disk is related to certain properties of the BCH product and to some notable features of the classical Bernoulli numbers: the two choices for $B_1$, the vanishing of $B_n$ for odd $n\geq 3$, and the equality $B_4=B_8$.

column5: Joshua A. Grochow; Youming Qiao; Katherine E. Stange; Xiaorui Sun
column6: On the complexity of isomorphism problems for tensors, groups, and polynomials V: over commutative rings
column7: Tensors over commutative rings naturally appear in number theory, geometry, and group theory. For example, $2\times 2\times 2$ tensors over $\mathbb{Z}$ form the starting point of Bhargava's celebrated works generalising Gauss's composition law (Bhargava, Ann. Math., 2004). Symmetric tensors over $\mathbb{Z}$ are central to the classification of Calabi--Yau threefolds (Yau, Commun. Pure Appl. Math., 1978; Wall, Invent. Math., 1966), geometric objects of significance in string theory. Additionally, tensors over finite commutative rings closely correspond to finite nilpotent groups of class 2 (Baer, Trans. Am. Math. Soc., 1938). In this work, we study isomorphism testing of tensors over commutative rings from a complexity-theoretic viewpoint, and its applications. Some of our main results are: 1. Let $\mathrm{R}$ be a commutative ring. We introduce two complexity classes: $\mathsf{3TI}_\mathrm{R}$ consisting of problems that are polynomial-time reducible to isomorphism problems of tensor products of three modules over $\mathrm{R}$, and $\mathsf{3FTI}_\mathrm{R}$ consisting of problems that are polynomial-time reducible to isomorphism problems of tensor products of three free modules over $\mathrm{R}$. 2. We show that some classical problems considered by Grunewald and Segal (ibid.), and the problem of classifying Calabi--Yau threefolds, are $\mathsf{3FTI}_\mathbb{Z}$-complete. We also show that many natural problems are complete for $\mathsf{3TI}_{\mathbb{Z}/p^e\mathbb{Z}}$. 3. We show that testing isomorphism of tensors in $\mathbb{Z}^2\otimes\mathbb{Z}^2\otimes\mathbb{Z}^2$ is polynomial-time equivalent to the principal ideal problem in algorithmic number theory. 4. We present an $N^{O((\log N)^{8/9})}$-time algorithm for testing isomorphism of finite nilpotent groups of class $2$ and odd order $N$.

column6: Partition statistics and universal mixed mock modular forms
column7: In this note, we construct combinatorial statistics in terms of partitions, overpartitions, and two-color partitions and relate the corresponding generating functions to the universal mock theta functions. Our framework primarily builds on two $q$-series identities of Fine.

column6: On Certain Congruences for Partition $k$-Tuples with $5$-Cores
column7: Let $A_{t,k}(n)$ denote the number of partition $k$-tuples of $n$ with $t$-cores. Using fifth-order modular equations and the Atkin $U_5$-operator, we prove the congruences $A_{5,125i+21}(25n+r)\equiv 0 \pmod{5^3}$ for $r\in\{9,14,19,24\}$, $A_{5,125i+41}(25n+r)\equiv 0 \pmod{5^3}$ for $r\in\{19,24\}$, and $A_{5,125i+111}(125n+r)\equiv 0 \pmod{5^4}$ for $r\in\{39,64,89,114\}$, which were stated by Tang \cite{tang2025iterative}.

column6: Cyclotomic polynomials with trinomial irreducible factors over finite fields
column7: We classify the pairs $(q,n)$, where $q$ is a prime power, $n>1$, and $\gcd(n,q)=1$, for which every irreducible factor of $Φ_n(x)$ over $\F_q$ has exactly three nonzero terms. The positive support exponents of these factors have a common greatest common divisor, which gives a unique reduction by a power substitution. The reduced degree is two in odd characteristic and belongs to $\{2,3,4\}$ in characteristic two; the cubic and quartic cases arise by scalar substitution from the layers of orders $7$ and $15$. This yields necessary and sufficient arithmetic conditions on $(q,n)$ and explicit factorizations. Among the classified families, precisely those arising from quartic bases have a divisor layer containing an irreducible factor with more than three terms.

column6: The distribution of $απ$ modulo one in $\mathbb{F}q(T)$: beyond Matomäki's exponent
column7: Let $α$ be an element of $\Fq((1/T))$ which is not in $\Fq(T)$. We ask how small $\nrm{απ}$ can be made when $π$ runs over irreducible polynomials, and write $θ(α)$ for the largest exponent $θ$ such that $\nrm{απ}<|π|^{-θ}$ has infinitely many solutions. The analogue of Matomäki's exponent, $θ(α)\ge\frac13$, was proved by Baier and the author, and it is the natural limit of \chg{methods based on} the Riemann Hypothesis. In this paper we go beyond it. For odd characteristic $p$ and $q$ large in terms of $p$ and $θ$, we prove that $θ(α)\geθ$ for every $α$ and every $θ<\sqrt2-1=0.414\ldots$, and for every $θ<\frac12$ when $α$ has bounded partial quotients. The main tools are an exact count of points in affine subspaces of $\Fq[T]$, a splitting of these subspaces into long arithmetic progressions, and the results of Sawin and Shusterman on the Möbius function along such progressions.

column6: A power-saving asymptotic for a Möbius-weighted GCD quadratic form
column7: For the Möbius-weighted quadratic form $T(N)=\sum_{m,n\leq N}μ(m)μ(n)(m,n)^2/(mn)$, we prove that $T(N)=cN+O_{\varepsilon}(N^{2/3+\varepsilon})$ for every $\varepsilon>0$, where $c>0$ is given by an absolutely convergent series of finite Möbius sums multiplied by a convergent Euler product. The proof combines the classical Jordan-totient decomposition of the GCD kernel with a mean-value estimate that is uniform in a coprimality parameter. Grouping the resulting squares according to $\lfloor N/d\rfloor$ gives the error term and a nonnegative series for $c$.

column6: On the Distribution of Prime Squares and Its Applications
column7: We prove that, for every \(A>0\), all but \(O_A(X(\log X)^{-A})\) integers \(n<X\) satisfying \(n\equiv11\pmod{24}\) admit a representation \[ n=a^2+b^2+p^2, \] where \(p\) and \(a^2+b^2+1\) are prime and \((a,b)=1\). For ergodic averages along prime squares, we prove a universal divergence result for integrable functions, while establishing almost-everywhere convergence for near-integrable functions. We also quantify how the bounds used to establish convergence behave as one approaches integrability. Moreover, we prove endpoint improving and sparse bounds for the corresponding discrete averages, with an explicit Orlicz loss.

column6: On potential density of rational points on hyperkahler varieties
column7: In this paper, we prove that the rational points on hyperkähler varieties in each of the four known deformation families admitting a rational Lagrangian fibration are potentially dense. Furthermore, we give several applications and construct examples of hyperkähler varieties beyond these families satisfying the potential density property. Our approach is first to prove that rational points on hyperkähler varieties admitting two rational Lagrangian fibrations with distinct associated isotropic rays are potentially dense. We then construct a projective Shafarevich--Tate twist admitting two such fibrations, together with a dominant rational map from the twist to the original variety.

column6: Porosity in Diophantine approximation
column7: We provide a general framework for obtaining upper bounds on the packing dimension of certain sets arising from Diophantine approximation using the notion of porosity from geometric measure theory. In particular, the framework relies on showing that such sets are mean porous, as introduced by Koskela and Rohde (Math. Ann., 1997). As applications of our framework we show that: For $\varepsilon>0$ sufficiently small, the set of $d$-dimensional $\varepsilon$-badly approximable points has packing codimension comparable to $\varepsilon^{d}$ up to multiplicative constant. Any $C^{2}$ submanifold of $\mathbb{R}^{d}$ with bounded first and second partial derivatives intersected with the set of $d$-dimensional $\varepsilon$-badly approximable points has packing dimension strictly less than the dimension of the submanifold. For any matrix $A\in \mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$ satisfying certain Diophantine conditions, the set of points that avoid the $\varepsilon \|\mathbf{q}\|_{\infty}^{-\frac{n}{m}}$-neighbourhood of the orbit $\{A\mathbf{q} \mod \mathbb{Z}^{m}:\mathbf{q} \in \mathbb{Z}^{n}\}$ has packing codimension greater than $C_{A} \varepsilon^{m}$ for $C_{A}$ a constant depending on $A$ and $m$ only. \end{itemize}

column6: Cuspidal sheaves on the stack of L-parameters
column7: We introduce the notion of cuspidal coherent sheaves on the moduli stack of local L-parameters. We give a complete classification and relate them to Lusztig's cuspidal local systems (or character sheaves). Under the categorical local Langlands conjecture, these sheaves are expected to correspond to supercuspidal representations supported at basic points. We also construct semiorthogonal decompositions of the category of coherent sheaves on the moduli stack of L-parameters that conjecturally match the semiorthogonal decompositions of sheaves on $\mathrm{Bun}_G$ coming from the stratification by the Kottwitz set and Bernstein decomposition of representation categories.

column6: The Dilate Rollercoaster
column7: Given a finite subset $A\subseteq\mathbb{Z}$ and a multiset of non-zero integers $Λ=\{λ_1, \ldots, λ_k\}$, the dilate sum \[Λ\cdot A:=λ_1\cdot A+λ_2\cdot A+\cdots+λ_k\cdot A =\{λ_1a_1+\cdots+λ_ka_k: a_1, \ldots, a_k\in A\}.\] For a non-zero real number $r$, say that $Λ_2$ $r$-dominates $Λ_1$ if we can partition some of the elements of $Λ_2$ into blocks summing to the elements of $r\cdotΛ_1$. Then for all finite subsets $A\subseteq\mathbb{Z}$, $Λ_2\cdot A$ contains a translate of $r\cdot(Λ_1\cdot A)$, and hence $|Λ_1\cdot A|\le|Λ_2\cdot A|$ for all $A$. In a recent paper, Kravitz (arXiv:2606.27087) proves the converse: if $Λ_2$ does not $r$-dominate $Λ_1$ for any $r$, then there exists a finite set $A$ satisfying $|Λ_1\cdot A|>|Λ_2\cdot A|$. For example, $\{2, 3, 5, 7\}$ does not contain two disjoint subsets with a sum ratio of 7, and so there exists a finite $A\subseteq\mathbb{Z}$ for which $|A+7\cdot A|>|2\cdot A+3\cdot A+5\cdot A+7\cdot A|$. We extend Kravitz's method to apply it to multiple inequalities and multiple sets, showing that for multisets $Λ_{i,j}$ with $1\le i\le k$ and $1\le j\le\ell$, there exist finite sets $A_1, \ldots, A_\ell\subseteq\mathbb{Z}$ such that for all $1\le i<k$ \[|Λ_{i,1}\cdot A_1+\cdots+Λ_{i,\ell}\cdot A_\ell| >|Λ_{i+1,1}\cdot A_1+\cdots+Λ_{i+1,\ell}\cdot A_\ell|\] provided there do not exist indices $1\le i_1<i_2\le k$ and a non-zero scalar $r$ such that $Λ_{i_2,j}$ $r$-dominates $Λ_{i_1,j}$ for all $1\le j\le\ell$. Along the way, we resolve the analogue of Nathanson's Problem 1 for his Theorem 4 (arXiv:1604.08940), as well as the problems in Section 1.4.3 of Kravitz's paper.

column6: On the Iwasawa invariants of admissible quadratic twists of elliptic curves at ordinary Eisenstein primes
column7: We study the Iwasawa $μ$- and $λ$-invariants of quadratic twists of rational elliptic curves at Eisenstein primes $p\geq 3$. We verify Greenberg's $μ=0$ conjecture for all such twists, which gives an Euler system free proof of Mazur's cotorsion conjecture, and study the $λ$-invariants when the twist is admissible in the sense of [GV00]. As a consequence, we prove the cyclotomic Iwasawa Main Conjecture and obtain the $p$-part BSD formulae in rank $0$ for admissible twists under mild conditions, covering many elliptic curves of potentially ordinary reduction.

column6: Spectral Beurling-Selberg Approximation and Applications to Effective Motivic Chebotarev-Sato-Tate Estimates
column7: We establish a spectral Beurling-Selberg approximation theorem on compact connected Riemannian manifolds for sets whose boundaries have finite upper Minkowski content. Our majorants and minorants have controlled spectral coefficients and explicit stability under Hausdorff perturbations, uniformly over families satisfying a common Minkowski content bound. We extend the construction to singular spaces arising from Riemannian submetries with basic mean curvature, and apply it to equidistribution on quaternionic Shimura varieties. Assuming the conjectural formalism of the specified motivic L-functions, including the motivic Riemann hypothesis, we develop effective Chebotarev-Sato-Tate estimates for fixed sets and varying families with controlled boundary geometry and Hausdorff variation, and describe how additional symmetries improve the error exponents. The proofs combine classical analytic methods with new methods from differential geometry, analytic geometry, and Riemannian spectral analysis. Applications include an asymptotic formula for a motivic analogue of Atkin-Serre estimates and tubular estimates for Picard-rank jumps of K3 surfaces via their transcendental motives.

column5: Sandro Bettin; Sary Drappeau; Jungwon Lee
column6: Central values of additive twists of automorphic $L$-series
column7: We study series $L(x,s):=\sum_n ρ(n)e^{2πi n x}/n^s$, where $ρ(n)$ are Fourier coefficients of an automorphic form $φ$ for a discrete cofinite subgroup $Γ\subset \mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ and $x\in\mathbb{R}$. Let $\mathfrak{b}\in\mathbb{R}\cup\{\infty\}$ represent a cusp of $Γ$. Ordering the orbit $Γ\mathfrak{b}$ by increasing denominators, we prove that the values $L(x,1/2)$ for $x\inΓ\mathfrak{b}$, suitably normalized, become equidistributed according to a standard complex Gaussian law, under natural assumptions on the Laplace eigenvalue of $φ$. Previously this was known either when $Γ=\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$ or when $φ$ is associated to a holomorphic cusp form. This applies in particular to central values at $s=1/2$ of additive twists of Maass form $L$-functions $\sum_{n\geq1}λ(n)e^{2πi n x}/n^s$, or to the Dirichlet-theta series $\sum_{n\geq1}χ(n)e^{2πi n^2 x}/n^s$.

column5: Sandro Bettin; Sary Drappeau; Jungwon Lee
column6: Limit theorems for cuspidal orbits on Fuchsian groups
column7: Let $Γ\subset \operatorname{SL}(2, \mathbb{R})$ be discrete, co-finite with cusps, and let ${\frak b}\in \mathbb{R}\cup\{\infty\}$ be a cusp of $Γ$. Let $f: Γ{\frak b} \to \mathbb{R}$ be a quantum modular form in the sense that the maps $$ φ_γ(x) = f(x) - f(γx) \qquad (x\in Γ{\frak b}, γ\in Γ) $$ extend to Hölder-regular functions. Under bounded moments assumptions of the shape $\sum_n n^{-2} \int |φ_{γ^n}(x)|^αd x < \infty$ for some $α>0$ and every fixed parabolic element $γ\in Γ$, we prove asymptotic formulas for the characteristic functions of the values $f(x)$ for $x\in Γ{\frak b}$, ordered by growing denominators. These yield Gaussian limits when $α>2$ and other stable limit laws under suitable further assumptions. This generalizes to Fuchsian groups the work of Baladi-Vallée on rational orbits of the Gauss map. In companion papers, we use this result, and in particular its flexible assumptions on $φ_γ$, to deduce limit theorems for automorphic $L$-series at the central point. One ingredient in our proof is a particular cuspidal acceleration of the Bowen-Series map, whose inverse branches admit a convenient parametrization, and for which we describe explicitly a natural extension.

column6: A conjecture on Galois groups and large fields
column7: Let $p$ be a prime number and let $K$ be a field such that $p$ is prime to the absolute Galois group $\operatorname{Gal}(K)$, in the sense that $p$ does not divide the degree of any finite Galois extension of $K$. We conjecture that $K$ is large in the sense of Pop: any smooth algebraic curve $C$ over $K$ with a $K$-rational point has infinitely many $K$-rational points. This conjecture would have some consequences in mathematical logic. For instance, it would imply the expected classification of stable fields of positive characteristic. We give some weak evidence for this conjecture. Specifically, suppose that $K$ is a perfect field and $\operatorname{Gal}(K)$ is prime to $p$. Then every abelian variety $A$ over $K$ has Zariski dense $K$-rational points, and if $C$ is a smooth curve of genus less than $7-p$ with at least one $K$-rational point, then $C$ has infinitely many $K$-rational points.

column6: On the modularity of residually reducible Galois representations of rank 2
column7: We use a new version of the Taylor--Wiles method, based on a tame analogue of the techniques introduced by Skinner--Wiles, to prove new modularity theorems for residually reducible Galois representations of rank 2 over totally real fields.

column6: Estimates of Lucas series and expansions in non-integer bases
column7: Special Fibonacci and Lucas type expansions proved useful to ``correct'' some theorems on the number of expansions in non-integer bases \cite{BaiKomLor2021, KomLorPed2024, KomLorPed2025}. The proof of a key lemma was non-constructive. It was made constructive in the Fibonacci case by giving a precise estimate of the growth of the partial sums of the series of the inverses of the Fibonacci numbers \cite{KomPed2025}. In this paper we extend this result to the general case.

column6: Joint universality of the Riemann zeta-function with arbitrary real shift parameters
column7: We prove that the shifts $ζ(s+id_jτ)$, $1\le j\le n$, are jointly universal for any nonzero real parameters $d_j$ with pairwise distinct absolute values. These restrictions are best possible. As an immediate consequence, we obtain generalized strong recurrence for arbitrary finite families of nonzero real parameters. Our proof uses Emsalem's generalization of the six exponentials theorem and a new variant of Pecherskii's rearrangement theorem.

column6: Iterated toric descent obstruction and homogeneous spaces over geometric global fields
column7: We study torsors under tori and groups of multiplicative type together with the obstruction they define to the existence of rational points in the setting of geometric global fields. Our methods give two new arithmetic applications: the iterated toric descent obstruction coincides with the toric decent obstruction and the toric obstruction is the only obstruction to the existence of rational points for homogeneous spaces of connected linear groups with either connected or abelian geometric stabilizers. These applications generalize some known results for classical global fields, due to Borovoi, Colliot-Thélène, and Sansuc, while exhibiting novel behaviors.

column5: Koustav Banerjee; Kathrin Bringmann; Bernhard Heim; Ben Kane
column6: On sign patterns of Fourier coefficients of theta quotients
column7: Motivated by conjectures of Schlosser and Zhou on sign patterns of Fourier coefficients of infinite products, we study two families of theta quotients and their positive integral powers. We determine asymptotic formulas for their Fourier coefficients and use them to obtain explicit eventual periodic sign patterns. Our results provide new instances of the sign phenomena observed by Schlosser and Zhou and illustrate how dominant cusps determine the resulting sign patterns. These results were formalized and verified in Lean by AxiomProver.

column6: Irrationality of values of $L$-functions for real Dirichlet characters
