For $L^2$-normalized local solutions at frequency $λ$, cubic integrals against smooth compactly supported weights tend to zero whenever the curvature is nonzero almost everywhere where the weight is nonzero. Finite-order nondegeneracy yields sharp polynomial decay rates. In particular, on closed surfaces with nowhere-vanishing curvature, we obtain the rate $O(λ^{-1/6})$, attained by spherical harmonics on the round sphere. This proves the cubic case of the Gaussian moment conjecture for all normalized real eigenfunctions on closed negatively curved surfaces. The local proof rests on an exact identity relating the reduced phase at a Fermat point to Gaussian curvature. On complete hyperbolic surfaces with positive systole, we also prove global $O((\logλ)^{-3/2})$ decay for $L^2$-normalized eigenfunctions and smooth weights with bounded covariant derivatives through order two, without assuming finite area.

column6: Cohen-Lenstra heuristics and vanishing of zeta functions for superelliptic curves over finite fields
column7: We prove a Cohen-Lenstra type result commenting on the distribution of class group structures amongst function fields of superelliptic curves over finite fields. We also prove a result commenting on the sparsity of such superelliptic curves whose zeta functions vanish at a fixed complex number. These results are proven via point-counting techniques on certain Hurwitz schemes generalizing techniques of Ellenberg-Venkatesh-Westerland and Ellenberg-Li-Shusterman. To obtain these point counts, We prove a unitary big monodromy theorem generalizing big monodromy theorems of Yu and Achter-Pries by appealing to an arithmeticity theorem of Venkataramana.

column6: The Multiplicity One Defect and Congruence-Modular Exponent Ratios
column7: We introduce a multiplicity one defect that quantitatively measures the failure of multiplicity one for the Jacobian of the Shimura curve \(X^D(M)\) attached to an indefinite rational quaternion algebra of discriminant \(D\) and level \(M\), localized at a maximal ideal of the Hecke algebra. By constructing a certain lattice inside the local Tate module, we obtain an explicit upper bound for the defect in terms of congruences between eigenforms and the lattice-Tate module discrepancies associated with the individual newforms. We then show that the local ratio between the congruence exponent and the modular exponent of modular abelian varieties attached to newforms is bounded above by the multiplicity one defect. Finally, we examine the relation with the Gorenstein property and give an explicit example at level \(126\) where the local Hecke algebra is Gorenstein even though multiplicity one fails. In this example, we compute the multiplicity one defect to be \(3\), which is also the local congruence--modular exponent ratio.

column5: Timothy S. Trudgian; Sebastian Zuniga Alterman
column6: Low Lying Zeros of Dedekind Zeta Functions
column7: Let $K$ be a number field of degree $n_K$, and let $h(K)$ denote the smallest absolute value of the imaginary part of a non-trivial zero of its Dedekind zeta function $ζ_K$. In 1979, Hoffstein proved the unconditional bound $h(K)\leq 0.87+o(1)$ as $n_K\to\infty$. In a 1990 survey, Odlyzko announced the stronger bound $h(K)\leq 0.54+o(1)$ without proof. No improvement on Hoffstein's bound has since appeared with a published proof. We construct a comparison kernel from a linear combination of three identities and show that Hoffstein's original parameters give $h(K)<0.825$ for sufficiently large $n_K$. We generalise Hoffstein's method via Stechkin's trick and prove $h(K)<0.58$ for all sufficiently large $n_K$, giving the best proved estimate to date. Moreover, $ζ_K$ has at least $c n_K$ non-trivial zeros with imaginary part in $[0,0.58]$, counted with multiplicity, for some $c>0$ and $n_K$ large enough.

column6: On bass orders in division algebras
column7: A result by F.-T. Tu dating from 2011 states that the orders in a local matrix algebra of dimension four that can be written as a finite intersection of maximal orders are those having an Eichler Gorenstein closure. In a more recent paper, we gave a similar characterization for orders with a Bass Gorenstein closure. More precisely, we prove that these orders are the ones that can be written as a ghost intersection, i.e., the set of points defined over the base field of an intersection of maximal orders that is defined over a field extension. Although we proved this result only for the local four-dimensional matrix algebra, the statement makes sense also for a local quaternion division algebra, since the latter turns into a matrix algebra when we extend the base field to an even degree extension. In this work, we prove an analog of our previous result in the latter setting.

column6: Zero density in short strips and short-interval bounds toward Hypothesis S
column7: We deduce zero-density estimates in short vertical strips from short-interval moments of globally tempered automorphic $L$-functions, by adapting the large-value estimate of Guth and Maynard and the Type II zero argument of Maynard and Pratt to the framework of Ye and Zhang. For the Riemann zeta function, we obtain $N_ζ(σ;T,T+T^a)\ll T^{15a(1-σ)/(3+5σ)+\varepsilon}$ for $2/3\le a\le1$ and $7/10\leσ\le4/5$, improving Ye--Zhang's exponent in the interior of this range. Combining the localized density bound with the recent quasi-Riemann theorems, we estimate smoothed prime-power sums with phase $\exp(2πiαn^β)$ on intervals of length $K^δ$. For $0<β<13/20$, we obtain a power saving whenever $\max\{17/30,1-β\}<δ<1$; in particular the square-root phase admits every $δ>17/30$. A revised transform estimate retains both the stationary spread and the Fourier width $K/L$. For example, the bound at $β=1/2$, $δ=3/5$ is $K^{15/26+\varepsilon}$, uniformly for frequencies $mα$ with $1\le m\le K^{1/10}$. We also retain power savings for certain self-dual $GL(2)$ twists and self-dual $GL(3)$ cusp forms, without assuming Ramanujan. All three applications have explicit frequency dependence.

column6: Nonlinear twists of Rankin-Selberg coefficients in the eigenvalue aspect
column7: Let $g$ be a fixed primitive Hecke--Maass cusp form, and let $f$ vary with spectral parameter $k_f=K$, at a fixed level and with trivial nebentypus. We study smooth sums of $λ_f(n)λ_g(n)e(αn^β)$ for fixed real $α\ne0$. The crucial input is the smooth spectral second moment of Lau, Liu, and Ye, for which the window length can be taken to be $L=K^{1/3+a}$ for arbitrarily small fixed $a>0$. We show that, for every $κ>0$, there is $β_0>0$ such that the sum is $O(K^{2/3+κ}X^{1/2})$ for $1\le X\le K^2$ and $0<β\leβ_0$. We give a detailed Baire category argument which makes the dependence on the smooth weight uniform through one finite derivative norm. A second argument keeps the phase explicit, applies Voronoi summation and shifted convolution estimates, and gives the numerical bound $O(K^{423/224+(5/7)β+\varepsilon})$ at $X=K^2$ for $0<β<5/32$.

column6: Universal Shift Congruences for Weighted Permutation Sequences
column7: The involution numbers $1,1,2,4,10,26,\ldots$ repeat modulo $3$, $5$ and $7$. We explain this, and many similar patterns, by one rule. Many sequences count permutations in which every cycle of length $m$ carries a weight $w_m$ (involutions, derangements, "sets of lists", and many others in the OEIS). Writing $A(n)$ for such a count, the rule is $A(n+k)\equiv A(n)A(k)$ modulo $\mathrm{lcm}(n,k)$. It generalizes our earlier proof of the case modulo $k$ for one such sequence, but now it holds for all weights at once, as a coefficientwise congruence between universal polynomials, and we find the largest modulus that works for the universal polynomials, $nk/\mathrm{rad}(\gcd(n,k))$, and show that nothing larger does. We then show that passing from $k$ to $pk$ behaves like raising to the $p$-th power modulo a high power of $p$, with a sharp exponent for the polynomials, which gives $A(p^r)\equiv(w_1+(p-1)w_p)^{p^{r-1}}$ modulo $p^r$ for odd $p$, and explains why the prime $2$ is special. A family of sequences defined by Lagrange inversion fits the same framework, which proves Bala's conjecture for the whole family (the single sequence A278070 had been proved earlier by an automated system) and the divisibility observed in the entries A251568 and A251569. As further applications we prove OEIS conjectures of Richman, Hanna, van Hoeij and Bala (A227937), and the theorems apply to 101 OEIS sequences, whose congruences are recorded in a supplementary catalogue. Higher-order versions of the content formula are treated in a separate paper.

column6: Iwasawa cohomology of pseudorigid families of $(\varphi,Γ)$-modules
column7: We study the Iwasawa cohomology complex attached to a pseudorigid family of $(\varphi, Γ)$-modules and prove coadmissibility of its cohomology groups, perfectness and compatibility with base change. We apply this result to give another proof of perfectness of the Herr complex in pseudorigid family. We also use it to prove perfectness of Selmer complexes and obtain a result on variation of ranks of Selmer groups in analytic family.

column6: A note on the $p$-adic inhomogeneous Littlewood conjecture
column7: Bugeaud, Haynes and Velani (2011) resolved a metric version of the $p$-adic Littlewood conjecture. We establish a fully inhomogeneous generalisation of their result, as well as a partially inhomogeneous generalisation of a result of Harrap and Haynes (2013) in the more general mixed setting.

column6: $6$ powers of $2$ in the Linnik--Goldbach problem
column7: Linnik's approximation to Goldbach's conjecture concerns the representation of sufficiently large even integers as the sum of two primes and a bounded number of powers of two. We prove that $6$ powers of $2$ suffice unconditionally and that $5$ suffice under the GRH, improving previous works.

column6: Tribonacci numbers that are palindromic concatenations of two distinct repdigits
column7: Let $(T_n)_{n\ge1}$ be the Tribonacci sequence, defined by $T_1=T_2=1$, $T_3=2$, and $T_n=T_{n-1}+T_{n-2}+T_{n-3}$ for $n\ge4$. In this paper, we study the Tribonacci numbers whose decimal representation is a palindromic concatenation of two distinct repdigits, that is, numbers of the shape $\overline{d_1\cdots d_1\,d_2\cdots d_2\,d_1\cdots d_1}$ with $1\le d_1\le9$, $0\le d_2\le9$, $d_1\ne d_2$. We prove that no Tribonacci number is a palindromic concatenation of two distinct repdigits. The proof combines lower bounds for linear forms in logarithms, the Baker-Davenport reduction method, and a finite computational verification.

column6: On the inverse Goldbach problem
column7: We establish two quantitative results concerning additive decompositions of the set $\mathbb{P}$ of primes. First, we prove that, if $A,B\subseteq\mathbb N$ have at least two elements and $A+B$ differs from the primes by only finitely many elements, then $$ \frac{\sqrt{x}}{\log x}\ll A(x),B(x) \ll \sqrt{x}. $$ Second, we show that, if $A,B,C\subseteq\mathbb N$ have at least two elements each, then $$ ((A+B+C)\mathbin{\bigtriangleup}\mathbb P)(x) \gg \frac{\sqrt{x}}{(\log x)^2}. $$ An analogous estimate is obtained for sumsets of $k\ge 3$ sets. The proofs use Montgomery's large sieve, Gallagher's larger sieve, a mean-value argument for a certain multiplicative function, and a submultiplicative sumset inequality.

column6: Solutions of $x_1^2+x_2^2-x_3^2=D$ with small $x_3$: a spectral approach
column7: We count the integral solutions of $x_1^2+x_2^2-x_3^2=D$ weighted by $Φ(x_3/M)$, for $M$ smaller than $\sqrt D$. Such solutions correspond to binary quadratic forms of discriminant $D$, and the count becomes a sum, over the geodesics of discriminant $D$, of a function of their distance to the point $i$. We evaluate it by the spectral theory of automorphic forms. Throughout, $θ=7/64$. For square $D=n^2$ the geodesics run from cusp to cusp, and Hecke theory reduces them to the single geodesic from $0$ to $\infty$. For every $n$ and both parities of $x_3$, we obtain an asymptotic formula with error $O(n^{1+θ+\varepsilon}M^{-1/2})$, using the Kim-Sarnak bound and the large sieve of Deshouillers and Iwaniec (and the theta group for the parity of $x_3$). It is non-trivial for $M\ge n^{71/96+\varepsilon}$. This improves the range $n^{5/6+\varepsilon}$ of the elementary method, and confirms the corrected main term of the author's earlier work. For non-square $D=f^2D_0$ the geodesics are closed. A Hecke relation for their traces reduces everything to the fundamental discriminant $D_0$. We obtain an error $O(D^{\varepsilon}f^{1+θ}D_0^{2/3}M^{-1/2})$, using the formulas of Duke-Imamoglu-Toth and Baruch-Mao together with the cubic moment bound of Young and of Andersen-Wu. For $D\equiv 5 \bmod 8$ this counts all solutions, and the range $M\ge D^{1/2-1/1332}$ of Friedlander and Iwaniec improves to $M\ge D^{4/9+\varepsilon}$. This paper was written in collaboration with Claude (Opus 5.5, High), an AI model developed by Anthropic.

column5: Bo Tan; Zhen Zhang; Qing-Long Zhou
column6: Poissonian Pair Correlation for Bernoulli Orbits
column7: Let \(α, β\in \mathbb{T} = \mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}\), and let \((ξ_n)_{n \ge 1}\) be independent random variables taking the values \(α\) and \(β\) with equal probability. We study the random walk \[X_n = ξ_1 + \cdots + ξ_n \pmod 1\] and present a deterministic Diophantine condition on \((α, β)\) that implies almost sure Poisson pair correlation. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first result providing explicit examples in this framework where the increment measure is purely discrete. The classical Fourier contraction method fails in this setting; a different approach is required. Our proof uses the parabolic geometry of returns to \(1\) and an exact covariance formula for overlapping blocks.

column6: Counting subspaces with prescribed Welch sums
column7: Let $q=2^n$ with $n=2m+1$ for an integer $m\ge1$, and let ${\mathbb F}_q$ be the finite field with $q$ elements. Let $W_n(x)=x^{2^m+3}$ be the Welch function on ${\mathbb F}_q$. For $1\le k\le n$ and $b\in{\mathbb F}_q$, denote by $N_{n,k}(b)$ the number of $k$-dimensional ${\mathbb F}_2$-subspaces $E$ of $\mathbb F}_q$ such that \[ \sum_{x\in E}W_n(x)=b. \] In this paper, we determine $N_{n,k}(b)$ for all $k$. The only nontrivial case is $k=3$, for which the answer is given in terms of a binary Kloosterman sum. As a consequence, we prove a recent conjecture of Hou and Zhao on the third-order sum-freedom of the Welch function.

column6: Coprime pairs with equal sum of divisors, assuming smooth shifted primes
column7: Let $h(x)$ be the number of pairs $1\le a<b<x$ with $\gcd(a,b)=1$ and $σ(a)=σ(b)$. Erdős Problem #824 asks whether $h(x)>x^{2-o(1)}$. By an argument of Pollack and Pomerance, this follows if for every fixed $δ>0$ there are $y^{1-o(1)}$ primes $p\le5y$ with $p+1$ free of prime factors exceeding $y^δ$. We write this implication out with explicit parameters and formalize it in Lean 4. We then check that the argument of the recent OpenAI preprint "Weighted dilation graphs, smooth shifted primes and totient fibers", which claims the corresponding statement for $p-1$, applies to $p+1$ after a change of sign in two of its sections. Consequently $h(x)=x^{2-o(1)}$, conditionally on the correctness of that preprint, which has not been refereed and whose main new estimates we have not independently verified.

column6: Post-critically finite polynomials in characteristic $p$
column7: It follows from the compactness of the connectedness locus that the locus of PCF polynomials in the moduli space of polynomials of degree d (at least 2) over the complex number is a countable union of zero-dimensional subvarieties. Over fields of characteristic p the analogous claim is certainly false, so it is natural to ask how large the components of the PCF locus can be. We show that the components of the PCF locus in the moduli space of polynomials of degree d over an algebraically closed field of characteristic p>0 have dimension at most d/p and that this bound is sharp, in the strong sense that for every p and d there are infinitely many distinct PCF components whose dimension is the greatest integer no greater than this bound (except in the case $p=d=2$).

column6: Bloch torsion and modular combinations of Nahm sums
column7: We construct a positive-definite symmetric integral $12\times12$ matrix $A$ such that, for every solution $Q$ of Nahm's equations $1-Q=Q^A$ with $Q_i\ne0,1$ for all $i$, the associated element $\sum_i[Q_i]$ is torsion in the Bloch group of $\mathbb{Q}(Q_1,\ldots,Q_{12})$. However, the Nahm sum $F_{A,B,C}(τ)$ is nonmodular for every $B\in\mathbb{Q}^{12}$ and $C\in\mathbb{Q}$. Thus the torsion condition for all solutions in Nahm's conjecture is not sufficient for the existence of a modular Nahm sum.

column6: The Goldbach exceptional set: an exponent 7/12 and conditional refinement
column7: Let \(E(X)\) count the even integers between \(4\) and \(X\) that are not sums of two primes. We combine Pintz's explicit formula for the major arcs with the exponential-sum estimate of Maynard, Pandey, and Radziwiłł to prove \(E(X)\ll_\varepsilon X^{7/12+\varepsilon}\) whenever all Dirichlet \(L\)-functions have a common fixed zero-free half-plane \(\Rea s>θ_0\), with \(θ_0<1\). The uniform \(7/8\) theorem reported in the OpenAI mathematics release supplies this input. Under the stronger hypothesis that every nontrivial Dirichlet zero has real part at most \(θ\), where \(1/2\leqθ\leq2/3\), we prove \[ E(X)\ll_{θ,\varepsilon}X^{g(θ)+\varepsilon}, \qquad g(θ)=\frac{θ(5-4θ)}{2(2-θ)}. \] Thus every fixed \(θ<2/3\) gives an exponent strictly below \(7/12\). The latter argument uses a classical fixed-modulus zero-density estimate and is independent of the new exponential-sum theorem.

column6: A linear independence criterion for $p$-adic Hurwitz zeta values at odd integers
column7: In this article, a new criterion is established to obtain the linear independence of some values of the $p$-adic Hurwitz zeta function at odd integers $s\geq 3$. We generalize a theorem of F.~Beukers, who gave, among others, an alternative proof---using Padé approximation theory---of a result originally due to F.~Calegari on the irrationality of the $p$-adic Riemann zeta value $ζ_p(3)$ for $p = 2, 3$. To prove our main theorem, we work in a general setting, where we construct and study new Padé approximants of Laurent series satisfying the functional equation $f(z) = f(1-z)$. This complements our previous work on the linear independence of $p$-adic polygamma values.

column6: Crystals and the parabolicity conjecture
column7: These notes introduce crystals and crystalline Dieudonné theory through the example of abelian varieties. After discussing $p$-divisible groups, $F$-isocrystals, slope filtrations, and overconvergence, we explain the parabolicity theorem for $F$-isocrystals and some of its applications to monodromy and Hecke orbits. Two appendices formulate research projects on isocrystals over formal schemes and on monodromy beyond the constant-slope setting. The exposition is intended for readers familiar with basic algebraic geometry and the étale and fppf topologies; prior knowledge of Witt vectors is helpful but not required.

column6: On the OpenAI proof that Landau-Siegel zeros do not exist
column7: A recent manuscript of OpenAI asserts that Landau-Siegel zeros do not exist. Here, we give a detailed account of its argument, arranged as a direct proof with explicit constants. There are absolute constants $q_0$ and $δ_0>0$ such that, for every primitive real Dirichlet character $χ$ of conductor $q\ge q_0$, every real zero $β\in(0,1)$ of $L(s,χ)$ satisfies $(1-β)\log q\geδ_0$, and one can take $q_0=10^{10}$ and $δ_0=3.0\times 10^{-3}$. Combined with a recent computation of Lu, Zaman, and Zhao, this result yields the bound $(1-β)\log q\ge 3.0\times 10^{-3}$ for every conductor $q\ge 3$. The proof is an interpolation determinant argument in the biquadratic field generated by $\sqrt{2}$ over the quadratic field attached to $χ$. A real zero close to one forces $χ(p)=-1$ for most primes $p$, and the Frobenius congruence at these primes makes a certain nonzero determinant divisible by higher powers of these primes than its Archimedean size allows. The underlying ideas are those of the OpenAI manuscript. The explicit constants, and the presentation, are new.

column6: Borel's computation of the ranks of $K$-theory revisited
column7: We reprove Borel's computation of the rank of the $K$-groups of rings of algebraic integers $\mathcal{O}_F$ for certain number fields, e.g., $F = \mathbb{Q}(μ_{l^k})$ for $l$ an odd regular prime number. The idea is to recover a simple formula for $l$-adic {é}tale cohomology groups of $\mathcal{O}_F$ in terms of Iwasawa theoretic objects without using Borel's result as an input.

column6: A trace Paley-Wiener theorem for $\mathrm{GL}_{n}(F)\backslash \mathrm{GL}_{n}(E)$, with $E/F$ a quadratic extension of non-Archimedean local fields
column7: We extend the classical trace Paley-Wiener theorem for $p$-adic reductive groups, given by Bernstein, Deligne and Kazhdan in 1986, to a relative case. That is when $E/F$ is a quadratic extension of $p$-adic fields, the main result is a scalar Paley-Wiener theorem for relative Bessel distributions on $\mathrm{GL}_n(F)\backslash \mathrm{GL}_n(E)$. These distributions are relative character of the form $$π\mapsto I_π(f), \ f\in C_c^\infty(\mathrm{GL}_n(E)),$$ as $π$ ranges over $\mathrm{GL}_n(F)$-distinguished irreducible tempered representations, and are constructed from a $\mathrm{GL}_n(F)$-invariant functional and a Whittaker functional. Using the local Langlands correspondence, and the base-change from a unitary group, we show that the relative characters can be described as elements of the "generic" Bernstein center of the unitary group $U(n)$.

column6: On strongly minimal asymptotic bases of order $h$ generated by powers of $2$
column7: Let $h\geq2$ be an integer and let $\mathbb{N}_0=W_1\cup\cdots\cup W_h$ be a partition into infinite sets. For $W\subseteq\mathbb{N}_0$, let $A(W)$ denote the set of all finite nonempty sums of distinct powers $2^w$ with $w\in W$. We give a necessary and sufficient condition for $A=A(W_1)\cup\cdots\cup A(W_h)$ to be a strongly minimal asymptotic basis of order $h$. This provides a complete answer to a problem posed by Nathanson in 1988.

column6: Monotonicity of Coefficients of Interpolated Multiple Zeta Values
column7: Let $ζ^t(\boldsymbol{k})=\sum_{d=1}^{r}S_d(\boldsymbol{k})t^{r-d}$ be the interpolated multiple zeta value of an admissible index $\boldsymbol{k}$ of depth $r$. We show the monotonicity property of coefficients $S_1(\boldsymbol{k})\ge\cdots\ge S_r(\boldsymbol{k})>0$. In the proof, we represent the coefficients as integrals over a common measure space and compares the integrands pointwise. As consequences, we determine the sign and vanishing of $ζ^{-1}(\boldsymbol{k})$ and locate the zeros of $ζ^t(\boldsymbol{k})$ in the closed unit disk.

column6: Non-vanishing of primitive cubic, quartic and sextic L-functions
column7: We establish lower bounds for the non-vanishing proportions of primitive cubic, quartic and sextic Dirichlet $L$-functions over $\F_q[T]$ in the non-Kummer setting. Adapting truncated-exponential techniques for shifted moments, we improve the cubic lower bound of David, Florea and Lalín and obtain positive lower bounds for quartic and sextic families. For each family, the lower limit of the non-vanishing proportion exceeds $e^{-e^{53}}$ as the conductor degree tends to infinity with $q$ fixed. We use a common choice of truncation parameters and explicitly control the exceptional sets. The cubic argument uses the published twisted first moment. We also establish uniform twisted first moments in the quartic and sextic cases, yielding an asymptotic formula for the sextic first moment.

column6: Counting Rational Points on a Certain Bihomogeneous Threefold
column7: Let $V\subset\mathbb P^2\times\mathbb P^2$ be the threefold $x_0y_0^2+x_1y_1^2+x_2y_2^2=0$, and let $U$ be the complement of its coordinate hyperplane sections. For the anticanonical height $H([\mathbf x],[\mathbf y])=|\mathbf x|^2|\mathbf y|$, evaluated on primitive integral representatives, we prove \[ N_U(B)=\frac{12π-14}{ζ(2)ζ(3)}B\log B+o(B\log B). \] The two projections combine lattice counting with uniform conic estimates. The main arithmetic step is an average of the fiber singular series, whose two main terms are related by Hilbert reciprocity. A moment estimate controls the full bad-prime part, and shape estimates permit the errors to be summed over the height region. We also check the leading constant with Peyre's constant.

column6: Amplified moments and a refinement of the quasi-Riemann hypothesis
column7: Recently, OpenAI announced a uniform $7/8$ zero-free half-plane for finite-order Hecke $L$-functions over $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-3})$, together with its transfer to Dirichlet $L$-functions. Assuming the analytic inputs of that work, we improve the boundary from $7/8=0.875$ to $8748867/10000000=0.8748867$ for the same families. The improvement combines a relaxed direct estimate with an amplified first moment of the reflected numerator, obtained from the existing fourth-moment estimate. A two-stage parameter argument yields the stated boundary without strengthening the inverse-moment estimate.

column5: Yuhang Cao; Sihuang Hu; Hexiang Huang; Mengrui Yang
column6: The Norm Spectrum of Barnes-Wall Lattices Below Twice the Minimum
column7: Let $Λ_m$ be the Barnes-Wall lattice of dimension $2^m$, normalized to have minimum squared norm $d_m:=2^{m-1}$. We determine its complete norm spectrum strictly between $d_m$ and $2d_m$, proving that, for every integer $m\ge1$, $\{\|x\|^2:x\inΛ_m,\ d_m<\|x\|^2<2d_m\}=\{2d_m-2^j:j\in\mathbb Z,\ \lceil m/2\rceil\le j\le m-2\}$. In particular, the norm spectrum in this interval is nonempty for $m\ge4$. The proof uses a Gaussian-integer model in which lattice automorphisms arising from Clifford unitaries transform a vector into a pair of coordinate subvectors in a lower-dimensional lattice. Divisibility of the differences of their squared norms and a matrix Parseval identity provide the arithmetic and averaging constraints needed for induction on $m$. Every listed norm is realized explicitly by a sum of two minimal vectors of the lattice.

column6: Bernoulli numbers and the integer group determinants of $C_p \times C_p$
column7: For a prime $p\ge7$, let $S(C_p\times C_p)$ be the set of integer group determinants and $e(p)$ the least exponent for which $p^{e(p)}\mathbf Z\subseteq S(C_p\times C_p)$. Let $r_p$ be the least integer $r\ge1$ satisfying $(2r+1)i>r(p-1)$ for every irregular pair $(p,2i)$ with $r\mid i$. We prove the unconditional inclusion $p^{p+3+2r_p}\mathbf Z\subseteq S(C_p\times C_p)$. Equality $e(p)=p+3+2r_p$ holds when Vandiver's conjecture holds for $p$ and $r_p\le(p-5)/2$, hence for every prime $7\le p<2^{31}$. The first exception to $e(p)=p+5$ is $p=103$, where $e(103)=116$. A polynomial obstruction from Bernoulli numbers supplies the lower bound, and circular units give the construction. For regular primes, we characterize the entire determinant set through explicit affine systems over $\mathbf F_p$ and principality conditions in $\mathbf Z[ζ_p]$. For regular $p\ge11$, prime cofactors cannot occur at valuation $p+3$; at valuation $p+4$ they have natural density $(p+1)/(hp^{(p-3)/2})$, where $h$ is the class number of $\mathbf Q(ζ_p)$. We also show that $p^{p+5}$ is the least absolute value of a nonzero $p$-divisible determinant for these regular primes.

column6: Post-critically finite polynomials over cyclotomic closures of number fields
column7: We prove that, for any number field K and and d at least 2, there are at most finitely many monic, centred, post-critically finite polynomials of degree d with coefficients in the extension of K by all roots of unity.

column6: Deformation and Symmetry in Two Hypergeometric Supercongruences
column7: We prove two supercongruence conjectures of Li--Long--Tu concerning truncated very-well-poised ${}_7F_6(1)$ series and Fourier coefficients of modular forms. The proofs are based on a common deformation method. By deforming the original truncated hypergeometric series to suitable terminating series, we are able to apply classical hypergeometric transformations together with Mishev's $W(D_5)$ symmetry. This reduces both problems to congruences for lower-rank hypergeometric sums that can be treated using the $p$-adic methods of Long--Tu--Yui--Zudilin. Although the two cases require different local arithmetic calculations, their global proof structure is the same. The resulting argument gives a unified explanation of these two supercongruences and suggests that the same deformation-and-symmetry method may apply more broadly.

column5: Luis Arenas-Carmona; Claudio Bravo; Ignacio Saavedra
column6: A quotient of the Bruhat-Tits building classifying maximal matrix orders over curves
column7: In a previous work, we defined a quotient graph of the Bruhat-Tits tree associated to the degree two special linear group over a local field whose vertex set is in correspondence with the maximal orders in a certain number of spinor genera. This graph has been applied to the study of the structure of some arithmetic groups, their presentations and their (co)homology groups. The genera of Eichler orders, which, for instance, are related to the problem of finding a basis that simultaneously splits two vector bundles with the same generic fiber, can often be described in terms of simpler genera via quotients. Furthermore, some embedding problems of orders can be studied via quotient graphs. These results provide a geometric framework for the study of maximal orders over function fields. In this article, we extend that construction to a higher dimensional setting through the use of singular chain complexes. Then we describe the set of vertices in this quotient that correspond to split maximal orders and the topology of the corresponding region of the quotient complex. More precisely, we show that these ``split vertices'' fall into a finite number of quotients of apartments by suitable subgroups of the corresponding Weyl group, the symmetric group. We relate these ``quotient apartments'' with the cuspidal sectors defined by previous authors who studied the quotient by the group of integral points of the special linear group. Both quotients are indeed related by a ramified cover that is unramified on cusps, as proved here.

column5: Linji Long; Yunchao Chi; Jinjiang Li; Min Zhang
column6: On Waring-Goldbach problem for two squares and higher powers
column7: Let $ν_1(n)$ and $ν_2(n)$, respectively, denote the number of representations of the natural number $n$ as the following form \begin{equation*} n=p_1^2+p_2^2+p_3^4+p_4^4+p_5^4+p_6^5+p_7^8, \end{equation*} and \begin{equation*} n=p_1^2+p_2^2+p_3^3+p_4^4+p_5^5+p_6^6+p_7^8, \end{equation*} where $p_1,\dots,p_7$ are primes in both above cases. In this paper, it is proved that $ν_1(n)\gg n^{43/40}(\log n)^{-7}$ holds for every sufficiently large integer $n$ subject to $n\equiv1\pmod2$ and $n\equiv\pm1\pmod3$. Moreover, we also establish that $ν_2(n)\gg n^{43/40}(\log n)^{-7}$ holds for every sufficiently large integer $n$ subject to $n\equiv1\pmod2$. These results improve and enhance the earlier work of Andrade [1] and Wang-Tian [17], respectively.

column5: Linji Long; Jinjiang Li; Min Zhang
column6: On a variant of the Piatetski-Shapiro prime number theorem
column7: Denote by $Π_γ(x)$ the number of primes $p \leqslant x$ such that $[p^{1/γ}]$ is also a prime. In this paper, it is proved that the expected asymptotic formula \begin{equation*} Π_γ(x)=\frac{γx}{(\log x)^2} (1+o(1)) \end{equation*} holds for $γ> 15/13$, which constitutes an improvement upon the previous result of Balog [2] who showed that the above asymptotic formula holds for $γ> 6/5$.

column5: Joey Glampe; Aryaman Joshi; Swagat Malla; Matthew Richey; Matthew Wright
column6: Polynomial Identities for Generalized Fibonacci Sequences
column7: The Fibonacci, Lucas, and Pell sequences satisfy certain families of ``polynomial'' identities. While a few members of these families are well-known, we are not able to find a general statement of these identities in the mathematical literature. We show that such polynomial identities exist for many generalized Fibonacci sequences, and we classify sequences that have these identities obtained by two distinct approaches. One approach uses the Girard-Waring formula, while the other relies on Binet's formula and linear algebra.

column6: Kitaoka's conjecture for real cyclotomic fields
column7: We prove Kitaoka's conjecture for all real cyclotomic fields, i.e. for fields of the form $\mathbb{Q}(ζ_k+ζ_k^{-1})$ where $ζ_k$ is a primitive $k$th root of unity. More precisely, we show that such a field admits a universal classical ternary quadratic form if and only if it is a real quadratic field.

column6: How iterated sumsets grow under the assumption of small doubling
column7: Let $K>1$ be a real number and let $A\subsetneq \mathbb Z$ be a finite and nonempty subset. Suppose $|A+A|<K|A|$. A fundamental open problem is to characterize the size of higher iterated sumsets $nA = A+\cdots+A$ ($n$-fold sumset). In 2004, Terry Tao formally posed the problem of determining the optimal growth function governing iterated sumsets of small-doubling sets. In this manuscript, we give a solution to this long-standing open problem for large enough $n$.

column6: Proof of Two Conjectural $q$-Supercongruences Related to Van Hamme's $\mathrm{(G.2)}$ Supercongruence
column7: In this paper, we prove two conjectures concerning parametric $q$- supercongruences related to Van Hamme's $\mathrm{(G.2)}$ supercongruence. First, we confirm Tang\rq s conjecture \cite[Conjecture $4.1$]{Tang G2} by establishing the corresponding congruences modulo $[m]Φ_m(q)^2$. Second, we prove a conjecture of Wang and Xu \cite[Conjecture $2$]{WangXu24}, extending their $q$-supercongruence modulo $Φ_m(q)^5$ to modulo $[m]Φ_m(q)^4$ when $m\equiv1\pmod4$.

column6: Exact Rank of the Largest Good Lattice Point Matrix
column7: We prove that for every integer $n>2$ the largest good lattice point matrix $U_n=[u_h:h\in H_n]$, whose columns are generated by all integers $h<n$ coprime to $n$, has rank exactly $\varphi(n)/2+1$. The upper bound follows from the pairing identity $u_h+u_{n-h}=(n,\dots,n,2n)^{\top}$. For the lower bound the columns are centered and the resulting orbit under the multiplicative group $(\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z})^{\times}$ is analysed by means of odd Dirichlet characters; the essential arithmetic input is the non-vanishing of $\sum_{a}a\,ψ(a)$ for odd primitive characters $ψ$, which is equivalent to Dirichlet's theorem $L(1,ψ)\neq 0$.

column6: Overlap distributions under the Gibbs measure of a Haar model of $\log|ζ|$ on and near the critical line
column7: We study the Gibbs measure of $H(h) = \Re\sum_{p^{j} \leq X}U_{p}^{j}/(j p^{j(σ+ i h)})$, a random field modeling large values of the log-modulus of the Riemann zeta function on and near the critical line, where the $U_{p}$ are independent and uniformly distributed on the complex unit circle. Writing $t = \log \log T$, the cutoff $X$ and real part $σ$ may vary with $T$ subject to $T^{1/t^Φ} \leq X \leq T^{1/t^φ}$ and $0 \leq σ- 1/2 \leq C_σt^Φ/\log T$, for fixed $Φ\geq φ> 1/2$ and $C_σ > 0$. On $I_θ = [ - (\log T)^θ,(\log T)^θ]$, define the Gibbs measure $G_{β,σ,T}^{\mathrm{H}}(\mathrm{d}h) := e^{βH(h)}\mathrm{d}h/\int_{I_θ}e^{βH(h')}\mathrm{d}h'$. For every fixed $θ> - 1$ and inverse temperature $β> 0$, the limiting joint distributions of correlations (overlaps) among points sampled from this measure are determined after averaging over the Haar phases. At and below $β_{c}(θ) = 2\sqrt{1 + (θ\vee 0)}$, the limiting two-overlap distribution is concentrated at $q_{0} = |θ\wedge 0|$. Above this threshold, it assigns masses $β_{c}(θ)/β$ and $1 - β_{c}(θ)/β$ to $q_{0}$ and $1$, respectively, and the limiting joint overlap distribution is described by a Poisson-Dirichlet process of parameter $β_{c}(θ)/β$. Approximate Ghirlanda-Guerra identities are shown to hold uniformly for bounded deterministic functions of the sampled positions. This paper is the first in a series devoted to extending these results to $\log|ζ|$ near the critical line.

column6: Bounds for (k,c) model functions over p-adic fields
column7: Let $F$ be a $p$-adic field, let $k,c\ge1$, and let $ρ$ be a $(k,c)$ representation of $\mathrm{GL}_{kc}(F)$: a complex representation of finite length whose wave front set has $(k^c)$ as its unique maximal orbit, and which admits a $(k,c)$ functional that is unique up to scaling. We prove that the functions in the $(k,c)$ model of $ρ$ are of moderate growth, by relating this model to the Zelevinsky model of $ρ$, and obtain as a consequence a bound for the restriction of these functions to the standard Levi subgroup associated with the composition $(c^k)$ of $kc$. As applications, we study convergence problems of several integrals involving $(k,c)$ models: integrals from the generalized doubling method, and a new family of integrals which extends the Rankin--Selberg integrals for Speh representations of Lapid and Mao.

column6: Examples of Bessel Functions of Order Zero Related to the Functional Equation of the Riemann Zeta Function
column7: In 2010, M. A. Chaudhry et al. introduced a class of functions Sigma satisfying an L^1-condition. They proved that every function phi in Sigma gives rise to the functional equation for the Riemann zeta function. They also provided an example of a function outside Sigma for which the functional equation still holds. In this paper, we present several examples of Bessel functions of order zero that do not belong to Sigma but nevertheless give rise to the functional equation for the Riemann zeta function. In particular, we show that J_0(a sqrt(x)), J_0(ax), and Y_0(x) exhibit this phenomenon.

column5: Yifan Luo; Tianze Wang; Haigang Zhou
column6: On trace-zero norm forms of orders of rational quaternion algebras with applications
column7: In this paper, by normalizing the trace-zero norm forms according to the parity of orders of definite rational quaternion algebras, we give an explicit formulation to the even Clifford correspondence followed by the reciprocity of ternary forms. We obtain an exact identity between ternary representation numbers and the number of elements of an order with prescribed reduced norm and trace, which applies to all orders without squarefreeness constraint on the reduced discriminant. Applications include a criterion for realizing ternary forms as trace-zero norm forms, a formula for traces of Brandt matrices in terms of representation numbers, and explicit theta series relations associated with local reciprocity. We also describe reciprocal orders and order chains, and interpret the ternary forms occurring in the congruent number problem through their associated quaternion orders.

column5: Xinyi Li; Shuochen Wang; Zimeng Ye; Alexandru Zaharescu
column6: Simultaneous Unimodularity of Positive Integer Matrices and Their Entrywise Cubes
column7: We solve an open problem posed by Richard Guy in his book Unsolved Problems in Number Theory. We prove that, for every integer $n\geq10$, there exist infinitely many $n\times n$ integer matrices $A$ such that every entry is $\ge2$ and $\det A=\det A^{[3]}=1$, where $A^{[3]}$ denotes the entrywise cube of $A$. The matrices may be chosen compatibly, so they can form the leading principal blocks of a single infinite positive integer array. The order-ten case is reduced to an inhomogeneous system consisting of one linear and one diagonal cubic equation. The circle method then provides infinitely many positive integral solutions. To pass from order $n$ to order $n+1$, we introduce a bordering construction that preserves the signed cofactor vectors of both the matrix and its entrywise cube. Iterating this construction yields the result in every order $n\geq10$.

column6: Survivor Set of Gauss Map with a Hole at $1$
column7: Let $T$ be the Gauss map. For each $α\in [0,1]$, let $E(α)$ be the survivor set consisting of all $x\in [0,1]$ whose orbit $\{T^k(x):k\ge 0\}$ never enters the interval $(α,1]$. We prove that the set-valued function $α\mapsto E(α)$ is increasing and locally constant almost everywhere. Moreover, we explicitly characterize all intervals where the function $α\mapsto E(α)$ remains constant. We also describe the points at which the map $α\mapsto E(α)$ is not locally constant. Further, we obtain the Hausdorff dimension of $E(α)$ for all $α\in [0,1]$. We prove that the function $α\mapsto \dim_H(E(α))$ forms a devil's staircase on $(0,1]$, but is not continuous at $0$. This discontinuity implies that the result of Raith [Acta Math. Univ. Comenian. 63 (1994), 39-53] fails for piecewise monotone interval maps with infinitely many branches. Finally, we give an application quantifying the set of points sharing identical $α$-continued fraction expansion and regular continued fraction expansion.

column6: Sharp Constants and Extremizers in Homogeneous Tree BMO
column7: We develop a finite-tree formalism for sharp inequalities on real-valued, mean-centered $\operatorname{L}^1$-BMO over homogeneous $q$-ary filtrations. A reduction theorem identifies local and global sharp constants with the supremum of finite-depth constants. Finite anchoring gives compact optimization problems and rational extremizers under rational piecewise-linear hypotheses, while stable centering shows that imposing zero root average preserves the supremum over all depths. The principal application is the absolute-value map: we construct centered examples in which taking absolute values increases the BMO seminorm and obtain bounds strictly below the universal factor $2$. Jensen-defect Carleson functionals and martingale-difference envelopes provide further applications, illustrating distinct anchoring mechanisms and the differences between finite-depth rationality, stabilization, and global attainment.

column6: The strong Ramanujan bound for Drinfeld modular forms
column7: The Ramanujan bound states that the degree of the trace of the $\mathfrak{p}$-Hecke operator on a space of weight $k$ Drinfeld cusp forms is at most $d(k-2)/2$, where $\mathfrak{p}$ is a prime of degree $d$ in $\mathbb{F}_q[T]$. We prove the strong Ramanujan bound, which states that at level 1, this bound can be improved to $d(k-(q+1))/2$. In addition, we classify when the strong Ramanujan bound is sharp; surprisingly, this turns out to depend on $\mathfrak{p}$ only through the parity of its degree. We also prove results related to the smallest slope of the Atkin operator and mod $p$ distributions of Frobenius polynomials of Drinfeld modules over finite fields.

column6: On the generalization of Christol's theorem to domains of finite type over finite fields
column7: We generalize Christol's theorem---which characterizes algebraic power series over a finite field in terms of automatic coefficient sequences---to completions of domains of finite type over a finite field~$\mathbb{F}_{q}$. Let $A$ be such a domain of dimension~$d$ and $\mathfrak{a}$ an ideal of depth~$d$. In the $\mathfrak{a}$-adic completion $\hat{A}$, choose an $\hat{A}$-regular sequence $\boldsymbol{x}=\{x_{1},\dots,x_{d}\}\subset\hat{\mathfrak{a}}$ and a set of representatives $E$ of $\hat{A}/(\boldsymbol{x})$ that is an $\mathbb{F}_{q}$-vector subspace consisting of algebraic elements. Every element $y\in\hat{A}$ then admits a unique expansion $y=\sum_{u\in\mathbb{N}^{d}}a_{u}x^{u}$ with coefficients $a_{u}\in E$. We prove that $y$ is algebraic over $A$ if and only if the coefficient sequence $\{a_{u}\}_{u\in\mathbb{N}^{d}}$ is $q$-automatic. The proof relies on a careful study of henselizations, which are shown to coincide with the algebraic closures inside the completions under certain conditions. As an application, we obtain a complete characterization of the automaticity of $β$-expansions for formal Laurent series over $\mathbb{F}_{q}$, answering questions posed by Hbaib--Mkaouar and Scheicher--Sirvent.
